NAME: Current tax liability
DESCRIPTION: According to IAS 1.54(n); IAS 12.5.

NAME: Curvature
DESCRIPTION: The additional potential loss beyond delta risk due to a change in a risk factor for financial instruments with optionality. In the standardised approach in the market risk framework, it is based on two stress scenarios involving an upward shock and a downward shock to each regulatory risk factor.

NAME: Cash on hand International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION:
Cash on hand International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) shall include holdings of national and foreign banknotes and coins in circulation that are commonly used to make payments.For Cash on hand International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) held for sale might apply.

According to ESA 2010 this includes "Monetary gold", which is indicated via the currency "XAU". See ESA 2010 paragraph 5.65 - 5.68.

NAME: Cash on hand national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION:
Cash on hand national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)  shall include holdings of national and foreign banknotes and coins in circulation that are commonly used to make payments.

According to ESA 2010 this includes "Monetary gold", which is indicated via the currency "XAU". See ESA 2010 paragraph 5.65 - 5.68.

NAME: Covered bond issuance
DESCRIPTION: A Covered bond issuance is a Covered bond issued under a Covered bond program.

NAME: Covered bond
DESCRIPTION: A Covered bond is a Debt security with underlying assets where, in the event of failure (of payment) of the issuer, the underlying assets are used on a priority basis for the reimbursement of the principal and payment of the accrued interest of the Covered bond (similar to the meaning of Directive 2009/65/EC, Article 52 (4)).

NAME: Covered bond programme relevant regime excess
DESCRIPTION: A covered bond programme is a form of credit transfer that involves the sale of a package of loans to a another financial institution for resale.

NAME: Covered bond programme
DESCRIPTION: A covered bond programme is a form of credit transfer that involves the sale of a package of loans to a another financial institution for resale.

NAME: Collateral given instrument Debt security issued assignment
DESCRIPTION: Collateral given instrument Debt security issued assignment is the combination of Collateral given instrument and Debt security issued that indicates which Debt security issued is protected by which Collateral given instrument.

NAME: Collateral given instrument Instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: Collateral given instrument Instrument assignment is an Instrument Collateral  instrument assignment where the collateral instrument role is a Collateral given instrument.

NAME: Collateral given instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Collateral given instrument is an Instrument role where the Instrument acts in the role of a Collateral given. Examples are a Financial guarantee given by the Reporting agent to a Customer.

NAME: Collateral given
DESCRIPTION: Collateral given is a Collateral role where the Collateral acts as Collateral given.

NAME: Collateral
DESCRIPTION: Collateral is an asset that is pledged to mitigate the credit risk that may arise from a contract that is not an Instrument.

NAME: Collateral received instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Collateral received instrument is an Instrument role where the Instrument acts in the role of a Collateral received. E.g. a Financial guarantee instrument received as a collateral for a Loan.

NAME: Collateral received
DESCRIPTION: Collateral received is a Collateral role where the Collateral acts as Collateral received.

NAME: Collateral role
DESCRIPTION: Collateral role is a role the Collateral may act in.

NAME: Loan debtor
DESCRIPTION: A Loan debtor is a Party role where the Party has the unconditional obligation to make repayments arising from a financial operation that is a Loan.

NAME: Loan
DESCRIPTION: A Loan is a Loan and Advance that is a Loan according to Regulation (EU) 1071/2013.

NAME: Lessor
DESCRIPTION: A Lessor is a Party role where the Party provides a Leasing good to a Lesee in a Finance lease.

NAME: Lessee
DESCRIPTION: A Lessee is a Party role where the Party receives a leasing good from a Lessor in a Financial lease.

NAME: Listed central bank and private sector company
DESCRIPTION: Listed central bank and private sector company is a Central bank and private sector company whose shares in the company are listed on a stock exchange.

NAME: Machinery and equipment collateral
DESCRIPTION: Machinery and equipment collateral is Non-registered collateral in the form of machinery and equiptment.

NAME: Master agreement Central counterparty assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement Central counterparty assignment is a Master agreement Party role assignment where the Party role is a Central counterparty.

NAME: Asset pool (subject to a Covered bond programme)
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool (subject to a Covered bond programme) is an Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer) that is associated with a Covered bond programme.

NAME: Asset pool Deposit assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool Deposit assignment is the combination of an Asset pool (subject to a securitisation and other credit transfer) and a Deposit that indicates which Deposit  is assigned to which Asset pool (subject to a securitisation and other credit transfer).

NAME: Asset pool Equity instrument that is not a security assignment
DESCRIPTION: Asset pool Equity instrument that is not a security assignment is the combination of Asset pool and Equity instrument that is not a security, that indicates which Equity instrument that is not a security is part of which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool Exchange tradable derivative position assignment
DESCRIPTION: Asset pool Exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of an Asset pool and an Exchange tradable derivative position that indicates which (part of an) Exchange tradable derivative position is comprised in which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool Instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: Asset pool Instrument assignment is the generalised combination of Asset pool and Instrument, that indicates which Instrument is part of which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer)
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer) is a pool of assets that is subject to a Securitisation or other credit transfer. It may comprise Instruments or (parts of) Security positions that have been removed from the Reporting agents' balance sheet, e.g. in case of a Traditional securitisation using an SSPE, where the Reporting agents acts in the role of a Servicer.

NAME: Asset pool Long balance sheet recognised security position assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool long balance sheet recognised security position assignment is the combination of an Asset pool and a long balance sheet recognised security postion that indicates which (part of a) long balance sheet recognised security postion is comprised in which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool Loan assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool Loan assignment is the combination of an Asset pool (subject to a securitisation and other credit transfer) and a Loan that indicates which Loan is assigned to which Asset pool (subject to a securitisation and other credit transfer).

NAME: Asset pool Non-balance sheet recognised security position assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool Non-balance sheet recognised security position assignment is the combination of an Asset pool and a Non-balance sheet recognised security postion that indicates which (part of a) Non-balance sheet recognised security postion is comprised in which Asset pool.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument not taken into possession
DESCRIPTION: Balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument obtained by taking possession is an asset that was not obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument taken into possession
DESCRIPTION: Balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument obtained by taking possession is an asset that was not pledged by the debtor as collatera or was pledged by the debtor as collaterall, but was  obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt, whether on a voluntary basis or as part of legal proceedings.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is a Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument where the applicable accounting standard in IFRS.

NAME: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent)
DESCRIPTION:
A Debt security issued (by the Reporting agent) is the combination of the  Debt security where the Reporting agent is the Debtor and the accounting classification that represents the financial liability side of the Debt security issued (by the reporting agent).

Please note: 
- The overall information about the Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) is in the entity type Debt security.
- The asset side of the bought back and/or retained part of the Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) is in the entity type Long debt security position.

NAME: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) Protection arrangement given assignment
DESCRIPTION: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) Protection arrangement assignment is the combination of Debt security issued and Protection arrangement stating which Debt security issued is protected by which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Issued debt security in the trading book International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Issued debt security in the trading book International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is an Issued debt security in the trading book where the applicable accountin standard is IFRS.

NAME: Other organisational unit
DESCRIPTION: An Other organisational unit is an Organisational unit that is not a Branch or an Investment vehicle / fund.

NAME: Other over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument
DESCRIPTION: An Other over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument that is not an Over the counter (OTC) Swap, Over the counter (OTC) Option or Over the counter (OTC) Forward.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Option other than Over the counter (OTC) Credit spread option
DESCRIPTION: Over the counter (OTC) Option other than Over the counter (OTC) Credit spread option is an Over the counter (OTC) Option that is not an Over the counter (OTC) Credit spread option.

NAME: Other over the counter (OTC) Swap
DESCRIPTION: An Other over the counter (OTC) Swap is an Over the counter (OTC) Swap that is not an Over the counter (OTC) Total return swap or an Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap.

NAME: Other overnight deposit
DESCRIPTION: An Other overnight is an Overnight deposit that is not a Transferable deposit.

NAME: Other party code
DESCRIPTION: Other party code is a Party code that is not a RIAD code nor an LEI.

NAME: Other party identifier
DESCRIPTION: Other party identifier is a code (different to the attribute Party identifier) of a Party that identifies the party in systems outside of the bank. It is a combination of a Party and a Party  identifier type.

NAME: Other provision
DESCRIPTION: A Other provisions is a Provision that is not Funds for general banking risk, Employee benefit, Resturcturing and Pending legal issues and tax litigation.

NAME: Other trade receivable
DESCRIPTION: An Other trade receivable is a Trade receivable other than Factoring.

NAME: Overnight deposit
DESCRIPTION:
An Overnight deposit is a Deposit fulfilling definition of Regulation (EU) 1071/2013, Annex 2, Part 2 Definitions of instrument categories, Table Instrument categories, 9.1 Overnight deposits:
Deposits which are convertible into currency and/or which are transferable on demand by cheque, banker’s order, debit entry or similar means, without significant delay, restriction or penalty. This item includes: 
(a) balances (interest-bearing or not) which are immediately convertible into currency on demand or by close of business on the day following that on which the demand was made, without any significant penalty or restriction, but which are not transferable; (b) balances (interest-bearing or not) representing prepaid amounts in the context of ‘hardware-based’ or ‘software-based’ e-money, e.g. prepaid cards; 
(c) loans to be repaid by close of business on the day following that on which the loan was granted.

NAME: Physical collateral
DESCRIPTION: Physical collateral is Collateral that is a material non-financial collateral.

NAME: Payment agent
DESCRIPTION:
Payment agent is a party role, where the party is fulfilling the duties of the payment agent in a syndicated loan or sub-participation. 

 It has to be reported to the ECB as a second servicer for the loan in certain circumstances.

NAME: Pending legal issues and tax litigation
DESCRIPTION: According to IAS 37.Appendix C. Examples 6 and 10.

NAME: Pension and other post-employment defined benefit obligation
DESCRIPTION: According to IAS 19.63; IAS 1.78(d); Annex V.Part 2.9.

NAME: Prudential consolidation group
DESCRIPTION: A Prudential consolidation group is an Internal consolidation group according to Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR), Part 1, Title II, Chapter 2, Section 2.

NAME: Performing debt security
DESCRIPTION: Performing debt security is a debt security that is classified performing.

NAME: Performing financial asset instrument debtor assessed
DESCRIPTION: A Performing financial asset instrument debtor assessed is a Financial asset instrument debtor assessed that is classified as performing according to FINREP, Annex V, part 2 (213)-(239).

NAME: Performing non-default financial asset instrument individually assessed
DESCRIPTION: A Performing non-default financial asset instrument individually assessed is a Non-default financial asset instrument individually assessed that is classified as performing according to FINREP, Annex V, part 2 (213)-(239).

NAME: Performing non-retail exposure class financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Performing non-retail exposure class financial asset instrument is a Non-retail exposure class financial asset instrument that is classified as performing according to FINREP, Annex V, part 2 (213)-(239).

NAME: Property, plant and equipment
DESCRIPTION:
Property, plant and equipment are tangible items that:
(a) are held for use in the production or supply of goods or services, for rental to others, or for administrative purposes; and 
(b) are expected to be used during more than one period. (IAS 16.6)

NAME: On demand deposit used for minimum reserve
DESCRIPTION: On demand deposit used for minimum reserve is an On demand deposit that is used to account for the minimum reserve to keep at the central bank, at the savings bank group, or similar.

NAME: Master agreement Clearing member assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement Clearing member assignment is a Master agreement Party role assignment where the Party role is a Clearing member.

NAME: Master agreement Entity role assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement Entity role assignment is the combination of a Master agreement and a Party role that indicates which Master agreement involves which Entity role.

NAME: Master agreement Financial contract assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement Financial contract assignment is the combination of a Master agreement and a Financial contract that indicates which Master agreement comprises which Financial contract.

NAME: Master agreement
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement is an arrangement that bundles Financial contacts and / or Protection arrangements.

NAME: Master agreement Non-qualifying central counterparty assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement Non-qualifying central counterparty assignment is a Master agreement Central counterparty assignment where the Central counterparty is a Non-qualifying central counterparty assignment.

NAME: Master agreement Qualifying central counterparty assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement Qualifying central counterparty assignment is a Master agreement Central counterparty assignment where the Central counterparty is a Qualifying central counterparty assignment.

NAME: Master agreement with a central counterparty
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement with a Central counterparty (CCP) is a Master agreement where a CCP is involved.

NAME: Master agreement with a clearing member
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement with a Central counterparty clearing member is a Master agreement via a Central counterparty clearing member.

NAME: Master agreement with a non-qualified central counterparty
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement with a non-qualifying central counterparty is a Master agreement with a central counterparty where the Central counterparty is a Non-qualifying central counterparty.

NAME: Master agreement with a qualifying central counterparty
DESCRIPTION: A Master agreement with a qualifying central counterparty is a Master agreement with a central counterparty where the Central counterparty is a Qualifying central counterparty.

NAME: Numeric rating system
DESCRIPTION: A Numeric rating system is a Rating system that assigns a (numeric) Probability of Default of a Party, Instrument or Debt security.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised debt security position
DESCRIPTION: A non-balance sheet recognised debt  security position is a debt security position that is not recognised in the balance sheet. A debt security position that is not recognised in the balance sheet is by default a long security position.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised equity or fund security position
DESCRIPTION: A non-balance sheet recognised equity or fund security position is a equity or fund security position that is not recognised in the balance sheet. A equity or fund security position that is not recognised in the balance sheet is by default a long security position.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is a Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position to which the IFRS accounting standard applies.

NAME: Non-retail exposure financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-retail exposure financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument that does not fulfil the definition of Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 123 Retail exposure. Consequently, such a Financial asset instrument must not be assigned to the Exposure class Retail exposure.

NAME: Non-self-employed natural person
DESCRIPTION: A Non-self employed natural person is a Natural person that is not self employed.

NAME: Non-syndicated contract nor sub-participation member instrument
DESCRIPTION: Non-syndicated contract nor sub-participation member instrument is a Loan that is not part of a syndicated loan or a sub-participation.

NAME: No registered Postal Code system party
DESCRIPTION: No registered Postal Code system party is a Party that uses an address that is a No registered Postal Code system address.

NAME: Natural person group role
DESCRIPTION: Natural person role is a Legal person role where the legal person type is a Natural person.

NAME: Non-renegotiated credit facility
DESCRIPTION: A Non-renegotiated credit facility is a credit facility where no renegotiation has taken place.

NAME: Non-renegotiated debt security
DESCRIPTION: A Non-renegotiated financial asset instrument is a debt security where no renegotiation has taken place.

NAME: Syndicated financial contract member
DESCRIPTION: Syndicated financial contract member is a Financial contract that is part of a Syndicated contract.

NAME: Synthetic securitisation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2(10):
‘Synthetic securitisation’ means a securitisation where the transfer of risk is achieved by the use of credit derivatives or guarantees, and the exposures being securitised remain exposures of the originator.

NAME: Synthetic securitisation involving an SSPE
DESCRIPTION: A Synthetic securitisation involving an SSPE is a Synthetic securitisation that involves a Securitisation Special Purpose Entity (SSPE).

NAME: Synthetic securitisation without involvement of an SSPE
DESCRIPTION: A Synthetic securitisation without the involvement of an SSPE is a Synthetic securitisation that does not involve a Securitisation Special Purpose Entity (SSPE).

NAME: Traditional securitisation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2 (9):
´Traditional securitisation’ means a securitisation involving the transfer of the economic interest in the exposures being securitised through the transfer of ownership of those exposures from the originator to an SSPE or through sub-participation by an SSPE, where the securities issued do not represent payment obligations of the originator.

NAME: Trade receivable Factor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Trade receivable Factor assignment is an Instrument Entity role where the Instrument is a Trade receivable and the Entity role is Factor.

NAME: Trade receivable Assigned debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Trade receivable Assigned debtor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Trade receivable and the Entity role is Assigned debtor.

NAME: Trade receivable collateral
DESCRIPTION: Trade receivable collateral is a Financial collateral that adheres to the definition of Trade receivable in paragraph 85(c) of part 2 of Annex V to the amended Implementing Regulation (EU) No 680/2014.

NAME: Trade receivable
DESCRIPTION:
A Trade receivable is a Loan fulfilling the definition of Annex V, Party 2.85(c):
‘Trade receivables’ shall include loans to other debtors granted on the basis of bills or other documents that give the right to receive the proceeds of transactions for the sale of goods or provision of services. This item shall include all factoring and similar transactions, like acceptances, outright purchase of trade receivables, forfaiting, discounting of invoice, bills of exchange, commercial papers and other claims where the reporting institution buys the trade receivables (both with and without recourse);

NAME: Term repurchase transaction
DESCRIPTION: A Term repurchase agreement instrument is a Repurchase agreement instrument with a specified maturity date.

NAME: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation
DESCRIPTION: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation is a securitisation tranche that is used in a synthetic securitisation.

NAME: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation with Securitisation Special Purpose Entity (SSPE)
DESCRIPTION: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation with SSPE is a Tranche in a synthetic securitisation where there is a Securitisation Special Purpose Entity involved.

NAME: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) being a deposit
DESCRIPTION: A Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) being a Deposit is a Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) that is a Deposit (acting as a collateral).

NAME: Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is a Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative position role to which the IFRS accounting standard applies.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative position role to which the nGAAP accounting standard applies.

NAME: Balance sheet netting
DESCRIPTION: A Balance sheet netting is the result of an operation in which financial Instruments are netted / off-set with each other for accounting purposes.

NAME: Property, plant and equipment taken into possession
DESCRIPTION: Property, plant and equipment taken into possession is Property, plant and equipment that was not pledged by the debtor as collateral, but was obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt, whether on a voluntary basis or as part of legal proceedings.

NAME: Perpetual debt security
DESCRIPTION: A Perpetual debt security is a Debt security with a fixed income and no maturity date.

NAME: Protection arrangement
DESCRIPTION: A Protection arrangement is an Arrangement that mitigates the credit risk that may arise from Contracts.

NAME: Protection arrangement given
DESCRIPTION: A Protection arrangement given is a Protection arrangement role where the Protection arrangement is given.

NAME: Protection arrangement given Exchange tradable derivative position assignment
DESCRIPTION: Protection arrangement given Exchange tradable derivative position assignment is the combination of Exchange tradable derivative position and Protection arrangement given  stating which Exchange tradable derivative position is offering protection for which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Protection arrangement given Instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: Protection arrangement given Instrument assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Protection arrangement given that indicates which Instrument is given to which Product arrangement given.

NAME: Protection arrangement received derived data
DESCRIPTION: Protection arrangement derived data is extra information about Protection arrangement that can be derived from other information in the model.

NAME: Protection arrangement received
DESCRIPTION: A Protection arrangement received is a Protection arrangement role where the Protection arrangement is received.

NAME: Protection arrangement role
DESCRIPTION: A Protection arrangement role is a role the Protection arrangement may act in.

NAME: Protection Protection provider assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Protection Protection provider assignment is the composition of a Protection arrangement and a Protection provider that indicates which Protection provider provides which Protection.

NAME: Protection provider
DESCRIPTION: A Protection provider is an Organisation role where the Organisation grants protection against a contractual agreed negative credit event and bears the credit risk of the negative credit event.

NAME: Partner enterprise assignment
DESCRIPTION: Partner enterprise assignment is the combination of a Central bank and private sector company and a Parent enterprise that indicates which Central bank and private sector company is a partner to which Central bank and private sector company in the sense of Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC.

NAME: Partner enterprise
DESCRIPTION: Partner enterprises are all enterprises which are not classified as linked enterprises and between which there is the following relationship: an enterprise (upstream enterprise) holds, either solely or jointly with one or more linked enterprises, 25 % or more of the capital or voting rights of another enterprise (downstream enterprise). (Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC)

NAME: Party code
DESCRIPTION: A party code is a code (different to the Party identifier) of a Party that identifies the party in systems outside of the bank. It is a combination of a Party and a Party code identifier.

NAME: Party
DESCRIPTION: A Party is an entity of interest.

NAME: Party previous period data
DESCRIPTION: A Party previous period data is information about a Party associated with the previous period. For example the Enterprise size that was calculated in the previous period.

NAME: Party role
DESCRIPTION: A Party role is a Party acting in a specific role. For example a Party acting in the role of Debtor (to a Loan).

NAME: Party risk data
DESCRIPTION: Party risk data is risk data related information associated with a Party.

NAME: Provisions associated with credit facility
DESCRIPTION: Provision associated with credit facility is provisions related to all commitments and guarantees, irrespective of whether their impairment is determined in accordance with IFRS 9 or their provisioning follows IAS 37 or whether they are treated as insurance contracts under IFRS 4. Under national GAAP based on BAD, provisions for ‘Commitments and guarantees given’ shall include provisions related to all commitments and guarantees.

NAME: Deposit-taking corporation
DESCRIPTION: The Deposit-taking corporations except the central bank subsector (S.122) includes all financial corporations and quasi-corporations, except those classified in the central bank and in the MMF subsectors, which are principally engaged in financial intermediation and whose business is to receive deposits and/or close substitutes for deposits from institutional units, hence not only from MFIs, and, for their own account, to grant loans and/or to make investments in securities.(Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, 2.75)

NAME: Natural person Key management personnel assignment
DESCRIPTION:
Natural person Key management personnel assignment is the combination of Key management personnel and Natural person that indicates which Natural person directly or indirectly influences the Key management personnel.

 If an individual is related to the entity based on the criteria stated above, all their close family members are also considered related parties. Close family members are defined as family members who are likely to influence, or be influenced by, that individual in their interactions with the entity (IAS 24.9). (via https://ifrscommunity.com/knowledge-base/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/#definition-of-a-related-party)

NAME: Natural person
DESCRIPTION: A Natural person is a Legal person which is a human being.

NAME: Non-European Union member party
DESCRIPTION: Non-European Union member party is a Registered postal code system party that uses an address that is a Non-European Union member address.

NAME: Not past due debt security
DESCRIPTION: Not past due debt security  is a debt security that is still performing.

NAME: Not past due financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: Not past due Financial instrument is a Financial asset instrument whose payments are considered to be on time.

NAME: Not significant risk transfer securitisation
DESCRIPTION: Not significant risk transfer securitisation is a Securitisation that does not establishes a significant risk transfer according to Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 243 (2) and Article 244 (2).

NAME: Offices and commercial premises collateral
DESCRIPTION: Offices and commercial premises collateral is a Commercial real estate and offices and commercial premises collateral that is Offices and commercial premises in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, i.e., where the debtor’s creditworthiness does not materially depend on any cash flow generated by the property, and the property’s value does not materially depend on the quality of the debtor

NAME: Offices and commercial premises not related to land collateral
DESCRIPTION: Offices and commercial premises not related to land collateral is an Offices and commercial premises collateral that is not related to land.

NAME: Offices and commercial premises related to land collateral
DESCRIPTION: Offices and commercial premises related to land collateral is an Offices and commercial premises collateral that is related to land.

NAME: Off-balance instrument Collateral given assignment
DESCRIPTION: Off balance instrument Collateral given assignment is the combination of an Off-balance instrument and a Collateral given that indicates which Off-balance instrument is given as which Collateral.

NAME: Off-balance instrument Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: Off balance instrument Collateral received assignment is the combination of an Off-balance instrument and a Collateral received that indicates which Off-balance instrument is protected by which Collateral.

NAME: Off-balance instrument
DESCRIPTION: An Off-balance instrument is an Instrument that is an Off-balance sheet item listed in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 575/2013 (CRR) except Credit facilities.

NAME: Other group of clients
DESCRIPTION: An Other group of clients is a Group of clients that is not a Group of connected clients or a Group of consolidated clients.

NAME: Other immaterial rights collateral
DESCRIPTION: Other immaterial rights collateral is Immaterial rights as collateral that is anything other than Software collateral.

NAME: Other commitment Creditor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Other commitment Creditor assignment is an Instrument Entity role where the Instrument is an Other commitment and the Entity role is Creditor.

NAME: Clearing member
DESCRIPTION: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Capital requirements for banks exposures to central counterparties (see https://www.bis.org/publ/bcbs227.pdf): A clearing member is a member of, or a direct participant in, a CCP that is entitled to enter into a transaction with the CCP, regardless of whether it enters into trades with a CCP for its own hedging, investment or speculative purposes or whether it also enters into trades as a financial intermediary between the CCP and other market participants.

NAME: Commodity collateral
DESCRIPTION: Commodity collateral is Non-registered collateral in the form of commodities, e.g. gold, silver.

NAME: Commodity risk factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION: The commodity risk factor for SA is a risk factor that takes into account the instrument's sensitivity to each type of commodity. (Article 325p) - Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council (CRR)

NAME: Commercial immovable property other than related to land (excluding agricultural land)
DESCRIPTION: Commercial Immovable property is a commercial real estate property other than related to land (excluding agricultural land).

NAME: Issued debt security in the trading book
DESCRIPTION: Issued debt security in the trading book is a Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) that are on the trading book.

NAME: Issued debt security in the trading book national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Issued debt security in the trading book national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is an Issued debt security in the trading book where the applicable accounting standard is nGAAP.

NAME: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) Traditional securitisation assignment
DESCRIPTION: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) Traditional securitisation assignment is the combination of Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) and Traditional securitisation assignment that indicates which Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) is assigned to which Traditional securitisation assignment.

NAME: Debt security
DESCRIPTION: A Debt security is a Security that is a debt instrument.

NAME: Debt security for national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Debt security for national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Debt security where the figures are applicable only to nGAAP.

NAME: Debt security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative
DESCRIPTION: A Debt security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative is a Security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative where the Security is a Debt security.

NAME: Debt security without underlying assets
DESCRIPTION: A Debt security without underlying assets is a Debt security that is not linked to underlying assets.

NAME: Debt security with underlying assets
DESCRIPTION: A Debt security with underlying assets is a Debt security where the cash flow of the Debt security is dependent on the cash flow of the underlying assets.

NAME: Default financial asset instrument individually assessed
DESCRIPTION:
A Default financial asset instrument individually assessed is a Financial asset instrument individually assessed that is in default according to Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 178 Obligor in default.
Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 178 Default of an obligor:
"In the case of retail exposures, institutions may apply the definition of default laid down in points (a) and (b) of the first subparagraph at the level of an individual credit facility rather than in relation to the total obligations of a borrower.".

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Non-balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is a Non-balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument where the applicable accounting standard in IFRS.

NAME: Entity group role
DESCRIPTION: Entity group role is an Entity role that is applicable to a group of legal entities.

NAME: Entity role
DESCRIPTION: An Entity role is a role a Party (or a subtype of Party) may act in.

NAME: Entity transaction role
DESCRIPTION: Entity transaction role is an Entity role where the role is specific to a transaction of the entity.

NAME: Equity or fund security borrowing and lending transaction component
DESCRIPTION: A Equity or Fund security borrowing and lending transaction component is a Security borrowing and lending transaction component where the Security is an Equity or Fund security.

NAME: Equity and fund security
DESCRIPTION: An Equity and fund security is a Security attesting the ownership of stocks.

NAME: Not past due debt security
DESCRIPTION: Not past due debt security  is a debt security that is still performing.

NAME: Not past due financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: Not past due Financial instrument is a Financial asset instrument whose payments are considered to be on time.

NAME: Non-renegotiated financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-renegotiated financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument where no renegotiation has taken place.

NAME: Not significant risk transfer securitisation
DESCRIPTION: Not significant risk transfer securitisation is a Securitisation that does not establishes a significant risk transfer according to Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 243 (2) and Article 244 (2).

NAME: Offices and commercial premises collateral
DESCRIPTION: Offices and commercial premises collateral is a Commercial real estate and offices and commercial premises collateral that is Offices and commercial premises in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 575/2013, i.e., where the debtor’s creditworthiness does not materially depend on any cash flow generated by the property, and the property’s value does not materially depend on the quality of the debtor

NAME: Deposit with agreed maturity
DESCRIPTION:
A Deposit with agreed maturity is an Other deposit fulfilling the definition of Regulation (EU) 1071/2013, annex 2, Part 2 Definitions of instrument categories, Table Instrument categories, 9.2. Deposits with agreed maturity:
Non-transferable deposits which cannot be converted into currency before an agreed fixed term or that can only be converted into currency before that agreed term provided that the holder is charged some kind of penalty. This item also includes administratively regulated savings deposits where the maturity related criterion is not relevant; these should be classified in the maturity band ‘over two years’. Financial products with roll-over provisions must be classified according to the earliest maturity. Although deposits with agreed maturity may feature the possibility of earlier redemption after prior notification, or may be redeemable on demand subject to certain penalties, these features are not considered to be relevant for classification purposes.

NAME: Asset backed security
DESCRIPTION:
An Asset backed security (ABS) is a Debt security with underlying assets where, in the event of failure (of payment) of the issuer, the underlying assets are not used on a priority basis for the reimbursement of the Asset backed security (ABS).
An asset-backed security (ABS) is a type of financial investment that is collateralized by an underlying pool of assets—usually ones that generate a cash flow from debt, such as loans, leases, credit card balances, or receivables. It takes the form of a bond or note, paying income at a fixed rate for a set amount of time, until maturity. For income-oriented investors, asset-backed securities can be an alternative to other debt instruments, like corporate bonds or bond funds.

NAME: Accounting consolidation group
DESCRIPTION: An Accounting consolidation group is an Internal consolidation group according to IFRS.

NAME: Advance Creditor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Advance Creditor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is an Advance and the Entity role is Creditor.

NAME: Fair-valued balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Fair valued balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument is a Balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument that is fair valued.

NAME: Fair-valued balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Fair-valued balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument is a Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument that is fair valued.

NAME: 30% Fair value decrease contingent encumbrance
DESCRIPTION: Contingent encumbrance refers to the additional assets which may need to be encumbered when the reporting institutions faces adverse developments triggered by an external event over which the reporting institution has no control (including a downgrade, decrease of the fair value of the encumbered assets or a general loss of confidence). In these cases, the reporting institution will need to encumber additional assets as a consequence of already existing transactions. The additional amount of encumbered assets shall be net of the impact of the institution’s hedge transactions against the events described under the aforementioned stressed scenarios. (Annext 17 (Asset Encumbrance) 4. Part C)

NAME: Fair-valued debt security issued
DESCRIPTION: A Fair-valued debt security issued is a Debt security issued that is fair valued.

NAME: Fair-valued balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative liability position is an Exchange tradable derivative position role which is Fair valued.

NAME: Fixed interest financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Fixed interest financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument with a fixed interest rate.

NAME: European Central Bank
DESCRIPTION: European Central Bank is a Central Bank that is the central bank of the European Union countries which have adopted the Euro as their currency. The ECB is an official EU institution at the heart of the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism.

NAME: Employee benefit
DESCRIPTION: Employee benefits are all forms of consideration given by an entity in exchange for service rendered by employees or for the termination of employment. (IAS 19)

NAME: Security collateral lending component
DESCRIPTION: Security collateral  lending component is a Security/Security collateral lending component where the security is represented directly by the Security collateral entity type.

NAME: Provisions associated with off-balance sheet item given
DESCRIPTION: Provision associated with off-balance sheet item given instrument is provisions related to all commitments and guarantees, irrespective of whether their impairment is determined in accordance with IFRS 9 or their provisioning follows IAS 37 or whether they are treated as insurance contracts under IFRS 4. Under national GAAP based on BAD, provisions for ‘Commitments and guarantees given’ shall include provisions related to all commitments and guarantees.

NAME: Provision
DESCRIPTION: A provision is a liability of uncertain timing or amount. (IAS 37)

NAME: Commercial immovable property related to land (excluding agricultural land)
DESCRIPTION: Commercial Immovable property is a commercial real estate property related to land  (excluding agricultural land).

NAME: Commercial real estate collateral
DESCRIPTION: Commercial real estate collateral is a Commercial real estate and offices and commercial premises collateral that is Real estate property other than residential property, offices and commercial premises, and which does affect the creditworthiness of the debtor (i.e. if the proceeds received from it affect the creditworthiness of the debtor.

NAME: Commercial real estate and offices and commercial premises collateral
DESCRIPTION: Commercial real estate and offices and commercial premises collateral is Real estate collateral that is not Residential real estate collateral, as according to the Q&A 2014_1214 : “For the purposes of the CRR, "commercial immovable property" encompasses any immovable property that is not a "residential property" within the meaning of Article 4(1)(75) of the CRR”.

NAME: Central bank and Corporation
DESCRIPTION: A Central bank and Corporation is an Central bank and private sector company authorized by the state to act as a single entity (a legal entity recognized by private and public law born out of statute; a legal person in legal context) and recognized as such in law for certain purposes.

NAME: Central bank
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 549/2013, 2.72:
Definition: the central bank subsector (S.121) consists of all financial corporations and quasi-corporations whose principal function is to issue currency, to maintain the internal and external value of the currency and to hold all or part of the international reserves of the country.

NAME: Central bank and private sector company
DESCRIPTION: An Central bank and private sector company is an Organisation that is not an International organisation or a General government.

NAME: Central bank and private sector company role
DESCRIPTION: A Central bank and private sector company role is a Central bank and private sector company acting in a specific role. Examples are Subsidiary, Joint venture or Associate.

NAME: Central counterparty client
DESCRIPTION: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - Capital requirements for banks exposures to central counterparties (see https://www.bis.org/publ/bcbs227.pdf): A CCP client is a party to a transaction with a CCP through either a clearing member acting as a financial intermediary, or a clearing member guaranteeing the performance of the client to the CCP.

NAME: Central government
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 549/2013, 2.114:
Definition: this subsector includes all administrative departments of the state and other central agencies whose competence extends normally over the whole economic territory, except for the administration of social security funds. Included in subsector S.1311 are those non-profit institutions which are controlled by central government and whose competence extends over the whole economic territory. Market regulatory organisations which are either exclusively or principally distributors of subsidies are classified in S.1311. Those organisations which are exclusively or principally engaged in buying, holding and selling agricultural or food products are classified in S.11.

NAME: Central government rating system
DESCRIPTION: A Central government rating system is an Issuer based rating system where the Issuer is a Central government.

NAME: Creditor
DESCRIPTION: A Creditor is a Party role where the Party is bearing the credit risk of a financial operation, other than the Protection provider.

NAME: Credit card debt Creditor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Credit card debt Creditor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Credit card debt and the Entity role is Creditor.

NAME: Credit card debt Loan debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Credit card debt Debtor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Credit card debt and the Entity role is Loan debtor.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative liability position is an Exchange tradable derivative position role which is not balance sheet recognised.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position to which the nGAAP accounting standard applies.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative asset position is an Exchange tradable derivative position role which is not balance sheet recognised.

NAME: Offices and commercial premises not related to land collateral
DESCRIPTION: Offices and commercial premises not related to land collateral is an Offices and commercial premises collateral that is not related to land.

NAME: Offices and commercial premises related to land collateral
DESCRIPTION: Offices and commercial premises related to land collateral is an Offices and commercial premises collateral that is related to land.

NAME: Off-balance instrument Collateral given assignment
DESCRIPTION: Off balance instrument Collateral given assignment is the combination of an Off-balance instrument and a Collateral given that indicates which Off-balance instrument is given as which Collateral.

NAME: Off-balance instrument Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: Off balance instrument Collateral received assignment is the combination of an Off-balance instrument and a Collateral received that indicates which Off-balance instrument is protected by which Collateral.

NAME: Off-balance instrument derived data
DESCRIPTION: Off-balance instrument derived data is extra information about Off-balance instrument that can be derived from other information in the model.

NAME: Off-balance instrument
DESCRIPTION: An Off-balance instrument is an Instrument that is an Off-balance sheet item listed in Annex I to Regulation (EU) 575/2013 (CRR) except Credit facilities.

NAME: Off-balance sheet item given instrument derived data
DESCRIPTION: Off-balance sheet item given instrument derived data is additional information about Off-balance sheet item given instrument.

NAME: Off-balance sheet item given instrument
DESCRIPTION: An Off-balance sheet item given instrument is an Instrument role where the Instrument acts as an Off-balance sheet item given.

NAME: Off-balance sheet item received instrument
DESCRIPTION: An Off-balance sheet item received instrument is an Instrument role where the Instrument acts as an Off-balance sheet item received.

NAME: Original lender
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2(20):
‘Original lender’ means an entity which, itself or through related entities, directly or indirectly, concluded the original agreement which created the obligations or potential obligations of the debtor or potential debtor giving rise to the exposures being securitised.

NAME: Organisational unit
DESCRIPTION:
A Organisational unit is a Party that is not (directly) documented by a legal document like a birth certificate for Natural persons, an article of association for limited (liability) companies.
Organisational units are individual building blocks that makes up an organisation. An Organisational unit constitutes one of the several functions within a company.
Contrary to a Legal person, Organisational units cannot, or only to a limited extend acquire legal rights and obligrations.

NAME: Organisation
DESCRIPTION: An Organisation is a Legal person which is an organized group of people with a particular purpose.

NAME: Organisation role
DESCRIPTION: An Organisation role is an Organisation acting in a specific role. For example an Organisation acting in the role of a Securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE).

NAME: Organisation risk data
DESCRIPTION: An Organisation risk data is additional risk related information about an Organisation.

NAME: Organisation without legal proceeding
DESCRIPTION: An Organisation without legal proceeding is an Organisation without a Legal proceedings status.

NAME: Organisation with legal proceeding
DESCRIPTION: An Organisation with legal proceeding is an Organisation with a Legal proceedings status.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument is a Financial liability instrument that is (at least to a certain extent) recognised in the balance sheet (of the reporting agent).

NAME: Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument where the applicable accounting standard in national GAAP.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised/ Non-balance sheet recognised security position
DESCRIPTION: A Balance sheet/ non-balance security position is a security position that might be recognised or not in the balance sheet.

NAME: Balance sheet recognised security position
DESCRIPTION: A balance sheet recognised security position is a security position that is recognised in the balance sheet.

NAME: Beneficiary
DESCRIPTION: A Beneficiary is a Party role where the Party derives advantages from a transaction.

NAME: Private sector company other than corporation
DESCRIPTION: An Central bank and private sector company other than corporation is an Central bank and private sector company that is not a Corporation. This type includes Non-profit institutions serving households according to the European system of accounts.

NAME: Past due debt security
DESCRIPTION: Past due debt security is a debt security past due in accordance with Part 2.48 of Annex V to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 680/2014.

NAME: Past due financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: Past due financial instrument is an Financial asset instrument whose payments are late, or past due.

NAME: Qualifying central counterparty (QCCP)
DESCRIPTION:
A qualifying central counterparty (QCCP) is an entity that is licensed to operate as a CCP by the relevant
regulator and that is based and prudentially supervised in a jurisdiction where the
relevant regulator has implemented domestic rules for financial market infrastructures that are consistent with the PFMIs by
CPMI-IOSCO. (Basel Committee on Banking Supervision Capital requirements for bank exposures to central counterparties)

NAME: Register of Institutions and Affiliates Database (RIAD) party code
DESCRIPTION: Register of Institutions and Affiliates Database (RIAD) party code is an Other party code that is the RIAD code.

NAME: Rolling stock collateral
DESCRIPTION: Rolling stock collateral is collateral in the form of "transit vehicles such as buses, vans, cars, railcars, locomotives, trolley cars and buses, and ferry boats, as well as vehicles used for support services." (see Buy America regulation (49 CFR Part 661.3).

NAME: Real estate collateral
DESCRIPTION: Real estate collateral is Registered collateral in the form of real estate.

NAME: Real estate collateral located in a member state
DESCRIPTION: Real estate collateral located in a member state is Real estate collateral inside the borders of a members state.

NAME: Real estate collateral not located in a member state
DESCRIPTION: Real estate collateral not located in a member state is Real estate collateral that is not located inside the borders of a member state.

NAME: Cash on hand International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION:
Cash on hand International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) shall include holdings of national and foreign banknotes and coins in circulation that are commonly used to make payments.For Cash on hand International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) held for sale might apply.

According to ESA 2010 this includes "Monetary gold", which is indicated via the currency "XAU". See ESA 2010 paragraph 5.65 - 5.68.

NAME: Deposit redeemable at notice
DESCRIPTION:
A Deposits redeemable at notice is an Other deposit fulfilling the definition of Regulation (EU) 1071/2013, Annex 2, Part 2 Definitions of instrument categories, Table Instrument categories, 9.3 Deposits redeemable at notice:
Non-transferable deposits without any agreed maturity which cannot be converted into currency without a period of prior notice; before the expiry the conversion into currency is not possible or possible only with a penalty. They include deposits which, although perhaps legally withdrawable on demand, would be subject to penalties and restrictions according to national practice (classified in the maturity band ‘up to and including three months’), and investment accounts without period of notice or agreed maturity, but which contain restrictive drawing provisions (classified in the maturity band ‘over three months’)

NAME: Deposit-taking corporation derived data
DESCRIPTION: Deposit-taking corporation derived data is additional information about a Deposit-taking corporation.

NAME: Deposit-taking corporation
DESCRIPTION: The Deposit-taking corporations except the central bank subsector (S.122) includes all financial corporations and quasi-corporations, except those classified in the central bank and in the MMF subsectors, which are principally engaged in financial intermediation and whose business is to receive deposits and/or close substitutes for deposits from institutional units, hence not only from MFIs, and, for their own account, to grant loans and/or to make investments in securities.(Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, 2.75)

NAME: Renegotiated credit facility without forbearance measure
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated credit facility with forbearance measure is a Renegotiated credit facility where forbearance measures have been applied.

NAME: Security collateral lending component Security collateral assignment
DESCRIPTION: Security collateral lending component Security assignment is the combination of the Security collateral ending component and the Security collateral that indicates which Security collateral has been lent out via the Security collateral  lending component.

NAME: Security debtor
DESCRIPTION: A Security debtor is an Organisation role where the Organisation has the unconditional obligation to make repayments arising from a financial operation that is a Security.

NAME: Security derived data
DESCRIPTION: Security derived data is derived information about a Security.

NAME: Security
DESCRIPTION: A Security is a Security and Exchange tradable derivative attesting credit or the ownership of stocks or bonds.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: A Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is a Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument where the applied accounting standard is IFRS.

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument that is not recognised in the balance sheet (of the reporting agent).

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Non-balance sheet recognised financial asset instrument where the applied accounting standard is national GAAP.

NAME: Foreign branch
DESCRIPTION: Foreign branch is a Branch that is located in another country then the Organisation of which it is a legally dependent part.

NAME: Foreign institutional unit
DESCRIPTION: Foreign institutional unit is an Institutional unit that is foreign branch of a credit institution which is a legally dependent part of the credit institution and is located in a country other than the country in which the credit institution is established.

NAME: Fair-valued balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position
DESCRIPTION: A Fair-valued balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative asset position is a Balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative position role which is Fair valued.

NAME: Master netting counterparty
DESCRIPTION: A Master netting counterparty is a Organisation role where the Organisation is involved in a Master netting agreement.

NAME: Movable property
DESCRIPTION: Movable property is an investment property that is movable, including cars, airplanes, ships, industrial and mechanical equipment (machinery, mechanical and technical equipment), inventories and commodities (merchandise, finished and semi-finished products, raw materials) and other forms of movable property.

NAME: Non-fair-valued balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position
DESCRIPTION: A Non-fair-valued balance sheet recognised exchange tradable derivative liability position is an Exchange tradable derivative position role which is not Fair valued.

NAME: Synthetic securitisation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2(10):
‘Synthetic securitisation’ means a securitisation where the transfer of risk is achieved by the use of credit derivatives or guarantees, and the exposures being securitised remain exposures of the originator.

NAME: Synthetic securitisation involving an SSPE
DESCRIPTION: A Synthetic securitisation involving an SSPE is a Synthetic securitisation that involves a Securitisation Special Purpose Entity (SSPE).

NAME: Synthetic securitisation without involvement of an SSPE
DESCRIPTION: A Synthetic securitisation without the involvement of an SSPE is a Synthetic securitisation that does not involve a Securitisation Special Purpose Entity (SSPE).

NAME: Traditional securitisation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2 (9):
´Traditional securitisation’ means a securitisation involving the transfer of the economic interest in the exposures being securitised through the transfer of ownership of those exposures from the originator to an SSPE or through sub-participation by an SSPE, where the securities issued do not represent payment obligations of the originator.

NAME: Trade receivable Factor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Trade receivable Factor assignment is an Instrument Entity role where the Instrument is a Trade receivable and the Entity role is Factor.

NAME: Trade receivable Assigned debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Trade receivable Assigned debtor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Trade receivable and the Entity role is Assigned debtor.

NAME: Other commitment Loan debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Other commitment Debtor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is an Other commitment and the Entity role is Debtor.

NAME: Other Immovable property
DESCRIPTION: Other Immovable property is an immovable property different than Residential and commercial immovable property.

NAME: Other intangible asset
DESCRIPTION:
An intangible asset is an identifiable non-monetary asset without physical substance.
As defined by IAS 38.8

(Monetary assets are money held and assets to be received in fixed or determinable amounts of money.)
As defined by IAS 38.8

https://www.investopedia.com/terms/i/intangibleasset.asp:
An intangible asset is an asset that is not physical in nature. Goodwill, brand recognition and intellectual property, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights, are all intangible assets. Intangible assets exist in opposition to tangible assets, which include land, vehicles, equipment, and inventory.

NAME: Branch
DESCRIPTION: A Branch is an Organisational unit that is a division or office of a (large) business or organisation, operating locally or having particular function.

NAME: Borrower
DESCRIPTION: A Borrower is a Party role where the Party borrows a good from a Lender.

NAME: Buyer
DESCRIPTION: A Buyer is a Party role where the Party buys goods (from a Seller).

NAME: Central Bank that is not the European Central Bank
DESCRIPTION: Central Bank that is not the European Central Bank is a Central Bank that is any other central bank but is not the European Central Bank (ECB).

NAME: Collateral annex
DESCRIPTION: A Collateral annex is an annex related to a Master agreement that specifies the conditions of the involved collateral.

NAME: Other financial collateral
DESCRIPTION:
Other financial collateral is Financial collateral other than Life insurance policy pledged collateral, Trade receivable collateral, Security collateral and Currency collateral.

Please note that this also deals with exposures to loans given as collateral by another company.

NAME: Other financial corporation
DESCRIPTION: A Other financial corporation is a Financial corporation that is not a Central bank and not a Credit institution.

NAME: Short balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) fiduciary item
DESCRIPTION: A Short balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) fiduciary instrument is  Short balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) that is a fiduciary item.

NAME: Short balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Short balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Short  balance sheet recognised security position reported under nGAAP.

NAME: Short balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Long  balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment is the combination of a Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment and a Prudential portfolio that indicates which security position is assigned to which Prudential portfolio.

NAME: Share capital repayable on demand
DESCRIPTION: According to IAS 32 IE 33; IFRIC 2; Annex V.Part 2.12.

NAME: Self-employed natural person
DESCRIPTION: A Self employed natural person is a Natural person that is self employed.

NAME: Seller
DESCRIPTION: A Seller is a Party role where the Party sells goods (to a Buyer).

NAME: Syndication or sub-participation member instrument Payment agent assignment
DESCRIPTION: Syndication or sub-participation member instrument Agent bank assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment that indicates if an instrument is part of a syndication loan or part of a sub-participation, which Agent bank is acting as the payment agent in that syndicate or sub-participation.

NAME: Syndication or sub-participation member instrument
DESCRIPTION: Syndication or sub-participation member instrument is a Loan (exluding repurchase agreement) that is part of either a syndicated loan or a sub-participation.

NAME: Single financial contract
DESCRIPTION: Single financial contract is a Financial contract that is not part of a Syndicated contract.

NAME: Equity or fund security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative
DESCRIPTION: A Equity or fund security postioin hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative is a Security postioin hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative where the Security is an Equity or fund security.

NAME: Equity instrument that is not a security Investor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Equity instrument that is not a security Investor assignment is the combination of an Equity instrument that is not a security and an Investor that indicates which Investor invested in which Equity instrument that is not a security.

NAME: Equity instrument that is not a security Issuer assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Equity instrument that is not a security Issuer assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is an Equity instrument that is not a security and the Entity role is Issuer.

NAME: Equity risk factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION: The equity risk factor for SA refers to the change in the value of the instrument, according to its pricing model. (Article 325o) - Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council (CRR)

NAME: Equity security
DESCRIPTION: An Equity security is an Equity and fund security in the form of an Equity instrument that is not a Fund.

NAME: Security Entity role assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Security or Exchange tradable derivative Entity role assignment is the combination of a Security or Exchange tradable derivative and an Entity role that indicates which Security or Exchange tradable derivative is associated with which Entity role.

NAME: Security and exchange tradable derivative
DESCRIPTION: A Security and exchange tradable derivative is a certificate attesting credit, the ownership of stocks or bonds, or the right to ownership connected with tradable derivatives.

NAME: Security or exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: A Security or exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of a Security or exchange tradable derivative and an Investor that indicates which Investor invests in which Security or exchange tradable derivative.

NAME: Security position hedged by Exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: Security position hedged by Exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of a Long/short balance sheet recognised security position and an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge that indicates which (portion of a) Security position is hedged by which Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge.

NAME: Security Issuer assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Security Issuer assignment is the combination of a Security and an Issuer that indicates which Security is issued by which Issuer.

NAME: Security lending component
DESCRIPTION: Security lending component is a Security/Security collateral lending component where the security is represented directly by the Security entity type.

NAME: State and local government and Social security funds
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 549/2013:
State government (excluding social security funds) (S.1312)
2.115 Definition: this subsector consists of those types of public administration which are separate institutional units
exercising some of the functions of government, except for the administration of social security funds, at a level
below that of central government and above that of the governmental institutional units existing at local level.
Included in subsector S.1312 are those non-profit institutions which are controlled by state governments and
whose competence is restricted to the economic territories of the states.
Local government (excluding social security funds) (S.1313)
2.116 Definition: this subsector includes those types of public administration whose competence extends to only a local
part of the economic territory, apart from local agencies of social security funds.
Included in subsector S.1313 are those non-profit institutions which are controlled by local governments and
whose competence is restricted to the economic territories of the local governments.
Social security funds (S.1314)
2.117 Definition: the social security funds subsector includes central, state and local institutional units whose principal
activity is to provide social benefits and which fulfil each of the following two criteria:
(a) by law or by regulation certain groups of the population are obliged to participate in the scheme or to pay
contributions; and
(b) general government is responsible for the management of the institution in respect of the settlement or
approval of the contributions and benefits independently from its role as supervisory body or employer.
There is usually no direct link between the amount of the contribution paid by an individual and the risk to
which that individual is exposed.

NAME: Swap provider
DESCRIPTION: A Swap provider is a Party role where the Party providing a Swap.

NAME: Syndicated contract
DESCRIPTION: Syndicated contract is the overall contract of the syndication in the administration of the lead arranger of the syndicated contract.

NAME: Syndicated financial contract member
DESCRIPTION: Syndicated financial contract member is a Financial contract that is part of a Syndicated contract.

NAME: Repurchase transaction Buyer assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Repurchase transaction Seller ssignment  is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Repurchase transaction and the Entity role is Buyer.

NAME: Repurchase transaction
DESCRIPTION: ‘Repurchase transactions (‘repos’) shall be transactions in which the institution receives or loans cash in exchange for financial assets sold/bought  at a given price under a commitment to repurchase the same (or identical) assets at a fixed price on a specified future date. - (FINREP Annex V, part 2.183-184 - Instructions)

NAME: Other loan
DESCRIPTION: An Other loan is a Loan that is not one of the following types: Financial lease, Trade receivable, Deposit, Credit card debt, Revolving credit, Overdraft, Reverse repurchase agreement loan.

NAME: Other non-financial asset
DESCRIPTION: An Other non-financial asset is a Non-financial asset that is not Goodwill, Tax asset, Investment property, Other intangible asset and Property, plant and equipment.

NAME: Other non-financial liability
DESCRIPTION: A Other non-financial liability is a Non-financial liability that is not a Tax liability or Share capital repayable on demand or Provision.

NAME: Other physical collateral
DESCRIPTION: Other non-registered collateral is Non-registered collateral other than Rolling stock collateral, Machinery and equipment collateral, Inventory collateral or Commodity collateral.

NAME: Other loan Creditor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Other loan Creditor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is of type Other loan and the Entity role is Creditor.

NAME: Other loan Loan debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Other loan Debtor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is of type Other loan and the Entity role is Loan debtor.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Credit spread option
DESCRIPTION: A Credit spread option (also known as a "credit spread") is an options contract that includes the purchase of one option and the sale of a second similar option with a different strike price. Effectively, by exchanging two options of the same class and expiration, this strategy transfers credit risk from one party to another.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative Buyer assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Derivative Buyer assignment is the combination of an Over the Counter (OTC) Derivative and a Buyer that indicates which Buyer buys which Over the counter (OTC) Derivative.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge where the applicable accounting standard is IFRS.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative role where the Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument acts as a hedge.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge where the applicable accounting standard is nGAAP.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument Collateral given assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument Collateral given assignment is the combination of a Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument and a Collateral given that indicates which Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument is assigned to which Collateral.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument is an Instrument in the form of a derivative that does not have an International securities identification number (ISIN).

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument Synthetic securitisation assignment
DESCRIPTION: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument Synthetic securitisation assignment is the combination of Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument and Synthetic securitisation assignment that indicates which Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument is assigned to which Synthetic securitisation assignment.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative Seller assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Derivative Seller assignment is the combination of a Seller and an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative that indicates which Over the counter (OTC) Derivative is sold by which Seller.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Forward
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Forward is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument through which two Parties agree to buy or sell an asset at a specified price on a future date.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Option
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Option is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument that offers the Buyer the opportunity to buy or sell the underlying asset.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap received as collateral instrument
DESCRIPTION: Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap received as collateral instrument is a Collateral received instrument where the instrument received as collateral is an Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap.

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Swap
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Swap is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument through which two Parties exchange the cash flows from two different financial instruments.

NAME: Credit card debt
DESCRIPTION: Credit card debt comprises credit granted to households or non-financial corporations either via delayed debit cards, i.e. cards providing convenience credit as defined below, or via credit cards, i.e. cards providing convenience credit and extended credit. Credit card debt is recorded on dedicated card accounts and therefore not evident on current or overdraft accounts. (Regulation (EU) 2021/379, Annex 2)

NAME: Credit facility Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Credit facility Collateral assignment is the combination of a Credit facility and a Collateral that indicates which Credit facility is assigned to which Collateral.

NAME: Credit facility Collateral received instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Credit facility Collateral received instrument assignment is the combination of a Credit facility and a Collateral received instrument that indicates which Credit facility is protected by which Collateral received instrument.
