A Term debt security is a Debt security that has a fixed maturity date and is not redeemable before that date.

This can be a term debt security that runs until its maturity date and is not redeemable before that date, or it can be a callable debt security that, when certain conditions are met, can be redeemed before its maturity date.

NAME: Security position
DESCRIPTION: A Security position is the combination of a Security and an Investor that indicates which Investor has invested in which Security.

NAME: Security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative
DESCRIPTION: A Security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative is the combination of a Long/Short balance sheet recognised security position and an Over the counter (OTC) derivative as a hedge that indicates which (portion of a Long/short balance sheet recognised security position is hedged by which Over the counter (OTC) derivative (acting in the role of an Over the counter (OTC) derivative as a hedge).

NAME: Security/Security Collateral lending component
DESCRIPTION: A Security/Security Collateral lending component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction component representing the Securities lent (to another Party), either as registered Security collateral, or directly as Security.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction cash as collateral component
DESCRIPTION: A Securities borrowing and lending transaction cash as collateral component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction including cash as collateral component that is cash as collateral.

NAME: Software collateral
DESCRIPTION:
Software as collateral is an Immaterial rights as collateral that is a legal concept that recognizes software as a form of intellectual creation that does not need a physical form, but grants the owner or creator exclusive rights to use, modify, distribute, or license it, subject to the intellectual property law.

See also IAS 38 for its usage as Property, Plant & Equipment or Other intangible non-financial assets.

NAME: Securities financing transaction (SFT) derived data
DESCRIPTION: Securities financing transactions (SFT) derived data is extra information about Securities financing transactions (SFT) that can be derived from other information in the model.

NAME: Securities financing transaction (SFT)
DESCRIPTION:
Securities financing transaction (SFT) allows investors and firms to use assets, such as the shares or bonds they own, to secure funding for their activities.
A securities financing transaction can be:
• a repurchase transaction - selling a security and agreeing to repurchase it in the future for the original sum of money plus a return for the use of that money
• lending a security for a fee in return for a guarantee in the form of financial instruments or cash given by the borrower
• a buy-sell back transaction or sell-buy back transaction
• a margin lending transaction

NAME: Significant currency 10% depreciation contingent encumbrance
DESCRIPTION: Contingent encumbrance refers to the additional assets which may need to be encumbered when the reporting institutions faces adverse developments triggered by an external event over which the reporting institution has no control (including a downgrade, decrease of the fair value of the encumbered assets or a general loss of confidence). In these cases, the reporting institution will need to encumber additional assets as a consequence of already existing transactions. The additional amount of encumbered assets shall be net of the impact of the institution’s hedge transactions against the events described under the aforementioned stressed scenarios. (Annext 17 (Asset Encumbrance) 4. Part C)

NAME: Significant risk transfer securitisation derived data
DESCRIPTION: Significant risk transfer securitisation derived data is additional information about Significant risk transfer securitisation that can be derived from other data already in the model.

NAME: Significant risk transfer securitisation
DESCRIPTION: Significant risk transfer securitisation is a Securitisation that establishes a significant risk transfer according to Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 243 (2) and Article 244 (2).

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap Collateral received instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION:
Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap Collateral received instrument assignment is the combination of Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap and Collateral received instrument that indicates which Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap is linked to which Collateral received instrument. 

Because there can be more than one CDS for one instrument, only one can become eligible as a guarantee for that instrument. However, all CDSes are linked here.

NAME: Security against Security borrowing and lending transaction
DESCRIPTION: A Security against Security borrowing and lending transaction is a Security borrowing and lending transaction where Securities are exchanged against Securities.

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate
DESCRIPTION:
A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate is an Internal group comprising all Subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates according the following definitions:
subsidiary: An entity that is controlled by another entity (see International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 10: Consolidated Financial Statement, Appendix A Defined terms)
joint venture: A joint venture is a joint arrangement whereby the parties that have joint control of the arrangement have rights to the net assets of the arragement (see International Accounting Standard (IAS) 28: Investments in Associates and Joint Venturs (3))
associate: An associate is an entity over which the investor has significant influence (see International Accounting Standard (IAS) 28: Investments in Associates and Joint Venturs (3))

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Other organisation role assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Central bank and private sector company role assignment is the combination of a Subsidiary, joint venture and associate and an Central bank and private sector company role that indicates which Subsidiary, joint venture and associate comprises which Central bank and private sector company role.

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Subsidiary assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Subsidiary assignment is a Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Other organisation role assignment where the Other organisation role is Subsidiary.

NAME: Subsidiary (of the reporting agent)
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary (of the reporting agent) is an Other organisation role where the Other organisation is controlled by the reporting agent (see International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 10: Consolidated Financial Statements, Appendix A Defined terms).

NAME: Securitisation and other credit transfer
DESCRIPTION: It comprises information on securitisations, as defined in Article 4.1(61) of Regulation No 575/2013, and other sales of assets. It refers to situations when: a.the securitisation or the credit transfer originates from the institution and the transferred assets are recognised in its balance sheet; or b. when the transferred assets are serviced by the institution, both in the case the securitisation or the credit transfer originates from the institution and in the case it originates from another entity.

NAME: Securitisation correlation trading portfolio (CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION: Securitisation correlation trading portfolio (CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach is a risk factor for standardised approach

NAME: Securitisation
DESCRIPTION: A Securitisation is a transaction or scheme, whereby the credit risk associated with an exposure or pool of exposures is tranched, having both of the following characteristics: (a) payments in the transaction or scheme are dependent upon the performance of the exposure or pool of exposures; (b) the subordination of tranches determines the distribution of losses during the ongoing life of the transaction or scheme (CRR, Article 4(1)(61)).

NAME: Securitisation non-correlation trading portfolio, (non-CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION: Securitisation non-correlation trading portfolio, (non-CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach is a risk factor linked to Asset backed securities

NAME: Securitisation tranche
DESCRIPTION: Securitisation tranche is a specific part of a securitised asset pool where one specific risk weight applies to.

NAME: Security against a fee borrowing and lending transaction
DESCRIPTION: A Security against a fee borrowing and lending transaction is a Security borrowing and lending transaction where one or more Securities are exchanged for a fee in return for a guarantee in the form of financial instruments or cash given by the borrower.

NAME: Advance Loan debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Advance Loan debtor assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is an Advance and the Entity role is Loan debtor.

NAME: Advance
DESCRIPTION:
An Advance is a Loan and Advance that is an Advance according to Annex V, Part 2.85(g):
‘Advances that are not loans’ shall include advances that cannot be classified as ‘loans’ according to the ECB BSI Regulation. This item shall include, among others, gross amounts receivable in respect of suspense items (such as funds that are awaiting investment, transfer, or settlement) and transit items (such as cheques and other forms of payment that have been sent for collection).

NAME: Aircraft collateral
DESCRIPTION: Aircraft collateral is Registered collateral in the form of an Aircraft (or parts of an Aircraft).

NAME: Investment property
DESCRIPTION: Investment property is property (land or a building or part of a building or both) held (by the owner or by the lessee under a finance lease) to earn rentals or for capital appreciation or both. (IAS 40.5)

NAME: Investment property taken into possession
DESCRIPTION: Investment property taken into possession is an investment property that was pledged by the debtor as collateral, but was obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt, whether on a voluntary basis or as part of legal proceedings.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position role
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative position role is an Exchange tradable derivative position acting in a specific role.

NAME: Exchange tradable future
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable future is an Exchange tradable derivative in the form of a future.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative liability position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative liability position is an Exchange tradable derivative asset or liability position role where the Exchange tradable derivative position acts in the role of a liability position.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative is a Security and  Exchange tradable derivative attesting the right to ownership connected with tradable derivatives.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge where the applicable accounting standard is IFRS.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge where the applicable accounting standard is nGAAP.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative position is a Security or Exchange tradable derivative position with an Exchange tradable derivative.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) fiduciary item
DESCRIPTION: Long balance sheet recognised security position  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) fiduciary asset is a Long balance sheet recognised security position  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment that is a fiduciary asset

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument is a Financial liability instrument that is not recognised in the balance sheet (of the reporting agent).

NAME: Non-balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Non-Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is a Non-Balance sheet recognised financial liability instrument where the applicable accounting standard in national GAAP.

NAME: Asset pool Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: Asset pool Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument assignment is the combination of Asset pool and Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument, that indicates which Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument is part of which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation)
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation) is an Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer) that is associated with a Securitisation.

NAME: (Reverse) Repurchase transaction Non-balance sheet recognised security position (received) assignment
DESCRIPTION: (Reverse) Repurchase transaction Non-balance sheet recognised security position assignment is the combination of a (reverse) Repurchase transaction  and Non-balance sheet recognised security position that is received in the (reverse) repurchase transaction.

NAME: Subsidiary (of the reporting agent)
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary (of the reporting agent) is an Other organisation role where the Other organisation is controlled by the reporting agent (see International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 10: Consolidated Financial Statements, Appendix A Defined terms).

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Associate assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Associate assignment is a Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Other organisation role assignment where the Other organisation role is Associate.

NAME: Security borrowing component
DESCRIPTION: A Securities borrowing component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction component representing the Securities borrowed (from another Party).

NAME: Security borrowing component Security Collateral assignment
DESCRIPTION: Security borrowing component Security Collateral assignment is the combination of the Security borrowing component and the Security collateral that indicates which Security collateral has been borrowed via the Security borrowing component.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction Borrower assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Security borrowing and lending transaction Borrower assignment is an Instrument Entity assignment where the Instrument is a Security borrowing and lending transaction Borrower assignment and the Entity role Borrower.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction component
DESCRIPTION: A Security borrowing and lending transaction component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction including cash as collateral component that is either a Security borrowed or a Security lent.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction including cash as collateral component
DESCRIPTION: A Securities borrowing and lending transaction including cash as collateral component is a component of a Securities borrowing and lending transaction, i.e. a Security borrowed, a Security lent or cash as collateral.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction
DESCRIPTION: A Security borrowing and lending transaction is a Securities financing transaction (SFT) where one or more Securities are exchanged (i.e. borrowed or lent) from one of the involved Parties to the other.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction Lender assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Security borrowing and lending transaction Lender assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Security borrowing and lending transaction and the Entity role is Lender.

NAME: Security collateral
DESCRIPTION: Security collateral is Financial collateral in the form of a Security.

NAME: Security collateral lending component
DESCRIPTION: Security collateral  lending component is a Security/Security collateral lending component where the security is represented directly by the Security collateral entity type.

NAME: Security collateral lending component Security collateral assignment
DESCRIPTION: Security collateral lending component Security assignment is the combination of the Security collateral ending component and the Security collateral that indicates which Security collateral has been lent out via the Security collateral  lending component.

NAME: Security debtor
DESCRIPTION: A Security debtor is an Organisation role where the Organisation has the unconditional obligation to make repayments arising from a financial operation that is a Security.

NAME: Security Entity role assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Security or Exchange tradable derivative Entity role assignment is the combination of a Security or Exchange tradable derivative and an Entity role that indicates which Security or Exchange tradable derivative is associated with which Entity role.

NAME: Security and exchange tradable derivative
DESCRIPTION: A Security and exchange tradable derivative is a certificate attesting credit, the ownership of stocks or bonds, or the right to ownership connected with tradable derivatives.

NAME: Security or exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: A Security or exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of a Security or exchange tradable derivative and an Investor that indicates which Investor invests in which Security or exchange tradable derivative.

NAME: Security position hedged by Exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: Security position hedged by Exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of a Long/short balance sheet recognised security position and an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge that indicates which (portion of a) Security position is hedged by which Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge.

NAME: Group
DESCRIPTION: A Group is a collection of Parties.

NAME: Immediate parent enterprise assignment
DESCRIPTION: Immediate parent assignment is the combination of a Central bank and private sector company and an Immediate parent that indicates which Central bank and private sector company has the role of immediate parent for which Central bank and private sector company.

NAME: Immediate parent enterprise
DESCRIPTION: Immediate parent enterprise is a Central bank and private sector company role that is the immediate parent of at least one Central bank and private sectore company via the Immediate parent enterprise assignment.

NAME: Immaterial rights as collateral
DESCRIPTION:
Immaterial rights as collateral is a Collateral that describe rights that are not financial and not material. 

An example of this are intellectual property rights.

NAME: Investment vehicle / fund
DESCRIPTION: An Investment vehicle / fund is a specific part of the balance sheet of an Organisation dedicated, and legally separated, for a specific purpose.

NAME: Investor
DESCRIPTION:
An Investor is a Party role where the Party invests in a position. 
Examples are the Investor in a Debt security position.
Please note that this definition also includes Investors as defined in Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2(11):
"'Investor' means a natural or legal person holding a securitisation position".

NAME: International securities identification number exchange tradable derivative
DESCRIPTION: An International securities identification number exchange tradable derivative is an Exchange tradable derivative with an International Securities Identification Number (ISIN).

NAME: International securities identification number security
DESCRIPTION: An International securities identification number security is a Security that has a (registered) International securities identification number (ISIN).

NAME: Issuer based rating system
DESCRIPTION: An Issuer based rating system is a (Credit) Rating system that quantifies the creditworthiness of a borrower in general terms.

NAME: Issuer
DESCRIPTION: An Issuer is an Party role where the Party acts in the role of an Issuer (of Securities). For example a Securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) issuing Asset-backed securities in the context of a Traditional securitisation, or a Credit institution issuing Debt securities.

NAME: Issue-based rating system
DESCRIPTION: An Issue based rating system is a (Credit) Rating system that evaluates the creditworthiness of a borrower with respect to a particular debt or financial obligation.

NAME: Joint venture (of the reporting agent)
DESCRIPTION: A Joint venture (of the reporting agent)  is an Other organisation role where the Other organisation is a joint arragnemetn whereby the parties (one of them being the Reporting agent) that have joint control of the arrangement have rights to the net assets of the arragement (see International Accounting Standard (IAS) 28: Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures (3)).

NAME: Life insurance policy pledged collateral
DESCRIPTION: Life insurance policies pledged collateral is a Financial collateral that adheres to the definition of Life insurance policies that are pledged to the lending institutions in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 575/2013.

NAME: Legal entity identifier party code
DESCRIPTION: Legal entity identifier party code is an Other party code that is the Legal entity identifier (LEI)

NAME: Legal person
DESCRIPTION: A Legal person is a Party which, under national law to which it is subject, can acquire legal rights and obligations.

NAME: Legal person role
DESCRIPTION: A Legal person role is a Legal person acting in a specific role.

NAME: Lender
DESCRIPTION: A Lender is a Party role where the Party borrows a good to a Borrower.

NAME: Land excluding agriculture collateral
DESCRIPTION: Land excluding agriculture collateral is an Offices and commercial premises not related to land collateral excluding agriculture.

NAME: Land including agriculture collateral
DESCRIPTION: Land including agriculture collateral is an Offices and commercial premises related to land collateral including agriculture.

NAME: Debt security borrowing and lending transaction component
DESCRIPTION: A Debt security borrowing and lending transaction component is a Security borrowing and lending transaction component where the Security is a Debt security.

NAME: Debt security Debtor assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Debt security Debtor assignment is the combination of a Debt security and a Debtor that indicates which Debtor is obliged to pay which Debt security.

NAME: Debt security for international financial reporting standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Debt security for international financial reporting standard (IFRS) is a Debt security where the figures are applicable only to IFRS.

NAME: Issued debt security in the banking book
DESCRIPTION: Issued debt security in the banking book is a Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) that is non-trading.

NAME: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) as a hedge
DESCRIPTION: Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) as a hedge is a Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) role where the Debt security issued (by the reporting agent) acts in the role of a non-derivative hedge.

NAME: Servicer
DESCRIPTION: A Servicer is a Party role where the Party is responsible for the administrative and financial management of a financial operation.

NAME: Securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE)
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2(2):
‘Securitisation special purpose entity’ or ‘SSPE’ means a corporation, trust or other entity, other than an originator or sponsor, established for the purpose of carrying out one or more securitisations, the activities of which are limited to those appropriate to accomplishing that objective, the structure of which is intended to isolate the obligations of the SSPE from those of the originator.

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate
DESCRIPTION:
A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate is an Internal group comprising all Subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates according the following definitions:
subsidiary: An entity that is controlled by another entity (see International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 10: Consolidated Financial Statement, Appendix A Defined terms)
joint venture: A joint venture is a joint arrangement whereby the parties that have joint control of the arrangement have rights to the net assets of the arragement (see International Accounting Standard (IAS) 28: Investments in Associates and Joint Venturs (3))
associate: An associate is an entity over which the investor has significant influence (see International Accounting Standard (IAS) 28: Investments in Associates and Joint Venturs (3))

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Joint venture assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Joint venture assignment is a Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Other organisation role assignment where the Other organisation role is Joint venture.

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Other organisation role assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Central bank and private sector company role assignment is the combination of a Subsidiary, joint venture and associate and an Central bank and private sector company role that indicates which Subsidiary, joint venture and associate comprises which Central bank and private sector company role.

NAME: Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Subsidiary assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Subsidiary assignment is a Subsidiary, joint venture and associate Other organisation role assignment where the Other organisation role is Subsidiary.

NAME: Securitisation and other credit transfer
DESCRIPTION: It comprises information on securitisations, as defined in Article 4.1(61) of Regulation No 575/2013, and other sales of assets. It refers to situations when: a.the securitisation or the credit transfer originates from the institution and the transferred assets are recognised in its balance sheet; or b. when the transferred assets are serviced by the institution, both in the case the securitisation or the credit transfer originates from the institution and in the case it originates from another entity.

NAME: Securitisation correlation trading portfolio (CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION: Securitisation correlation trading portfolio (CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach is a risk factor for standardised approach

NAME: Securitisation
DESCRIPTION: A Securitisation is a transaction or scheme, whereby the credit risk associated with an exposure or pool of exposures is tranched, having both of the following characteristics: (a) payments in the transaction or scheme are dependent upon the performance of the exposure or pool of exposures; (b) the subordination of tranches determines the distribution of losses during the ongoing life of the transaction or scheme (CRR, Article 4(1)(61)).

NAME: Securitisation non-correlation trading portfolio, (non-CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION: Securitisation non-correlation trading portfolio, (non-CTP) Risk Factor for standardised approach is a risk factor linked to Asset backed securities

NAME: Securitisation tranche
DESCRIPTION: Securitisation tranche is a specific part of a securitised asset pool where one specific risk weight applies to.

NAME: Security against a fee borrowing and lending transaction
DESCRIPTION: A Security against a fee borrowing and lending transaction is a Security borrowing and lending transaction where one or more Securities are exchanged for a fee in return for a guarantee in the form of financial instruments or cash given by the borrower.

NAME: Security against Security borrowing and lending transaction
DESCRIPTION: A Security against Security borrowing and lending transaction is a Security borrowing and lending transaction where Securities are exchanged against Securities.

NAME: Security borrowing component
DESCRIPTION: A Securities borrowing component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction component representing the Securities borrowed (from another Party).

NAME: Non-performing non-retail exposure class financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-performing non-retail exposure class financial asset instrument is a Non-retail exposure class financial asset instrument that is classified as non-performing according to FINREP, Annex V, part 2 (213)-(239).

NAME: Non-perpetual debt security
DESCRIPTION:
A Term debt security is a Debt security that has a fixed maturity date and is not redeemable before that date.

This can be a term debt security that runs until its maturity date and is not redeemable before that date, or it can be a callable debt security that, when certain conditions are met, can be redeemed before its maturity date.

NAME: Non-qualifying central counterparty
DESCRIPTION: A non-qualifying central counterparty (QCCP) is an entity that is not licensed to operate as a CCP, or is not permitted by the appropriate regulator/overseer to operate as such with respect to the products offered

NAME: Instrument Collateral assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Collateral assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Collateral that indicates which Instrument is protected by which Collateral.

NAME: Instrument Collateral instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Collateral  instrument assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Collateral received instrument or Collateral given instrument that indicates which Instrument is protected by which Collateral received instrument or which instrument is being protected by which Collateral given instrument.

NAME: Instrument Collateral received instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: Instrument Collateral received instrument assignment is an Instrument Collateral instrument assignment where the Collateral instrument is a Collateral received instrument and the Instrument assigned to it is not a Over the counter (OTC) Credit default swap.

NAME: Instrument Entity role assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Entity role assignment is the combination of an Instrument and an Entity role that indicates which Instrument is assigned to which Entity role.

NAME: Instrument hedged by Exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument hedged by exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of an Instrument and an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge that indicates which Instrument is hedged by which Exchange tradable derivative position, acting in a the role of an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge.

NAME: Instrument hedged by Over the counter (OTC) Derivative
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument hedged by Over the counter (OTC) Derivative is the combination of an Instrument and an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge that indicates which Instrument is hedged by which Over the counter (OTC) Derivative (acting in a the role of an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge).

NAME: Instrument
DESCRIPTION:
An Instrument is a product that establishes a financial relationship between a bank and its customer.
In the context of accounting such a financial relationship may be considered a financial asset or a financial liabilty or an off-balance sheet item.

NAME: Instrument Protection arrangement received assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Protection arrangement received assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Protection arrangement received that indicates which Instrument is related to which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Instrument Protection arrangement assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Protection arrangement assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Protection arrangement that indicates which Instrument is related to which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Instrument role
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument role is a role an Instrument may act in.

NAME: Instrument resulting from a Credit facility
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument resulting from a Credit facility is an Instrument that is created based on a Credit facility and not directly from a Financial contract.

NAME: Instrument resulting directly from a Financial contract
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument resulting directly from a Financial contract is an Instrument that is created directly as a result from a Financial contract without the involvement of a Credit facility.

NAME: Instrument Servicer assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Servicer assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Servicer that indicates which Instrument is serviced by which Servicer.

NAME: Institutional unit
DESCRIPTION:
An Institutional unit is a Group which is the composition of Branches according to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, 2.12 and 2.13.
Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, 2.12:
2.12 Definition: an institutional unit is an economic entity characterised by decision-making autonomy in the exercise of its principal function. A resident unit is regarded as constituting an institutional unit in the economic territory where it has its centre of predominant economic interest if it has decision-making autonomy and either keeps a complete set of accounts, or is able to compile a complete set of accounts.

NAME: Ship collateral
DESCRIPTION: Ship collateral is Registered collateral in the form of a Ship (or parts of a Ship).

NAME: Short balance sheet recognised security position derived data
DESCRIPTION: Short trading book security position derived data contains data about the Short trading book security position that can be derived from other information in the model.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)  is a Long balance sheet recognised security position  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment reported under nGAAP.

NAME: Suspense item
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) No 1071/2013, Annex 2, Part 2 Definitions of instrument categories, Table Intstrument categories, 7. Remaining assets:
Suspense items are asset balances held in the MFI balance sheet which are not booked in the name of customers but which nevertheless relate to customers’ funds, e.g. funds that are awaiting investment, transfer or settlement;

NAME: Rating grade Central bank and private sector company assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Rating grade Other organisation assignment is the combination of a Rating grade for issuer based rating system for non-central government and an Other organisation that indicates which Other organisation is assigned which Rating grade for issuer based rating system for non-central government.

NAME: Renegotiated credit facility
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated credit facility is a credit facility where a renegotiation has occured.

NAME: Renegotiated credit facility without forbearance measure
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated credit facility with forbearance measure is a Renegotiated credit facility where forbearance measures have been applied.

NAME: Renegotiated credit facility with forbearance measure
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated credit facility with forbearance measure is a Renegotiated credit facility where forbearance measures have been applied.

NAME: Renegotiated debt security
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated debt security  is a debt security where a renegotiation has occured.

NAME: Renegotiated debt security without forbearance measure
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated debt security without forbearance measure is a Renegotiated debt security  where no forbearance measure have been applied.

NAME: Non-qualifying central counterparty
DESCRIPTION: A non-qualifying central counterparty (QCCP) is an entity that is not licensed to operate as a CCP, or is not permitted by the appropriate regulator/overseer to operate as such with respect to the products offered

NAME: Non-renegotiated credit facility
DESCRIPTION: A Non-renegotiated credit facility is a credit facility where no renegotiation has taken place.

NAME: Non-renegotiated debt security
DESCRIPTION: A Non-renegotiated financial asset instrument is a debt security where no renegotiation has taken place.

NAME: Non-retail exposure financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-retail exposure financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument that does not fulfil the definition of Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 123 Retail exposure. Consequently, such a Financial asset instrument must not be assigned to the Exposure class Retail exposure.

NAME: Non-self-employed natural person
DESCRIPTION: A Non-self employed natural person is a Natural person that is not self employed.

NAME: Non-syndicated contract nor sub-participation member instrument
DESCRIPTION: Non-syndicated contract nor sub-participation member instrument is a Loan that is not part of a syndicated loan or a sub-participation.

NAME: No registered Postal Code system party
DESCRIPTION: No registered Postal Code system party is a Party that uses an address that is a No registered Postal Code system address.

NAME: Natural person
DESCRIPTION: A Natural person is a Legal person which is a human being.

NAME: Natural person group role
DESCRIPTION: Natural person role is a Legal person role where the legal person type is a Natural person.

NAME: Natural person Key management personnel assignment
DESCRIPTION:
Natural person Key management personnel assignment is the combination of Key management personnel and Natural person that indicates which Natural person directly or indirectly influences the Key management personnel.

 If an individual is related to the entity based on the criteria stated above, all their close family members are also considered related parties. Close family members are defined as family members who are likely to influence, or be influenced by, that individual in their interactions with the entity (IAS 24.9). (via https://ifrscommunity.com/knowledge-base/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/#definition-of-a-related-party)

NAME: Non-European Union member party
DESCRIPTION: Non-European Union member party is a Registered postal code system party that uses an address that is a Non-European Union member address.

NAME: Associate (of the reporting agent)
DESCRIPTION: An Associate is an Other organisation role where the Reporting agent (as an Investor) has significant influence over the Other organisation (see International Accounting Standard (IAS) 28: Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures (3)).

NAME: Assigned debtor
DESCRIPTION: An Assigned debtor is a Legal person role where the Legal person is either the Customer or the Ultimate debtor of a Factoring operation, depending on the type of Factoring operation, specifically with or without resourse).

NAME: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) being a financial guarantee
DESCRIPTION: A Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) being a Financial guarantee is a Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) that is a Financial guarantee.

NAME: Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE)
DESCRIPTION: A Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) is either a Financial guarantee or a Deposit acting as a collateral for a particular part of the underlying Pool of assets.

NAME: Tranche in a Traditional securitisation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2, (6):
´Tranche’ means a contractually established segment of the credit risk associated with an exposure or a pool of exposures, where a position in the segment entails a risk of credit loss greater than or less than a position of the same amount in another segment, without taking account of credit protection provided by third parties directly to the holders of positions in the segment or in other segments.

NAME: Transferable deposit
DESCRIPTION:
A Transferable deposit is an Overnight deposit fulfilling the definition of Regulation (EU) 549/2013, 5.80:
Definition: transferable deposits are deposits exchangeable for currency on demand, at par, and which are directly usable for making payments by cheque, draft, giro order, direct debit/credit, or other direct payment facilities, without penalty or restriction.

NAME: Transit item
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) No 1071/2013, Annex 2, Part 2 Definitions of instrument categories, Table Intstrument categories, 7. Remaining assets:
Transit items represent funds, usually belonging to customers, which are in the course of being transmitted between MFIs. Items include cheques and other forms of payment that have been sent for collection to other MFIs;

NAME: Tax asset
DESCRIPTION: Tax asset according to IAS 1.54(n); IAS 12.5, Accounting Directive art 17(1)(f); CRR art 4(1)(106)for IFRS: IAS 1.54(o); CRR art 4(1)(106) (for for nGaap).

NAME: Tax liability
DESCRIPTION: A Tax liability according to IAS 1.54(n);  IAS 12.5; CRR, Article 4(1)(108).

NAME: Registered postal code system party
DESCRIPTION: Registered postal code system party is a Party that uses an address that is in a Registered Postal Code system country.

NAME: Vega sensitivity
DESCRIPTION: The potential loss resulting from the change in value of a derivative due to a change in the implied volatility of its underlying.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised debt security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment
DESCRIPTION:
A Long balance sheet recognised  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment debt security position is a Long balance sheet recognised  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment security position where the Security is a Debt security.

If the position is in an Debt security issued (by the reporting agent), this contains the asset part.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised equity or fund security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment position
DESCRIPTION: An Long balance sheet recognised  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment equity or fund security position is a Long balance sheet recognised  prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment security position where the Security is an Equity or Fund security.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: Long balance sheet recognised security position collateral received assigment is the combination of Long balance sheet recognised security position and  collateral received stating which Long balance sheet recognised security position is protected by which Collateral.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Long balance sheet recognised security position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)  is a Long balance sheet recognised security position reported under IFRS.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position
DESCRIPTION: A long balance sheet recognised security position is security postion recognised in the balance sheet where the Investor holds the Security position.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Long balance sheet recognised security position national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)  is a Long balance sheet recognised security position reported under nGAAP.

NAME: Partner enterprise assignment
DESCRIPTION: Partner enterprise assignment is the combination of a Central bank and private sector company and a Parent enterprise that indicates which Central bank and private sector company is a partner to which Central bank and private sector company in the sense of Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment taken into possession
DESCRIPTION: A Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio Accounting classification assignment taken into possession is a  Long balance sheet recognised security position that was not pledged by the debtor as collateral, but was obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt, whether on a voluntary basis or as part of legal proceeding

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Long  balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment is the combination of a Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment and a Prudential portfolio that indicates which security position is assigned to which Prudential portfolio.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position prudential portfolio assignment risk data
DESCRIPTION: A Long balance sheet recognised security position risk data is risk related information about a Long balance sheet recognised debt security position.

NAME: Long balance sheet recognised security position protection arrangement received assignment
DESCRIPTION: Long balance sheet recognised security position Protection arrangement received assignment is the combination of Long balance sheet recognised security position Protection arrangement received and Protection arrangement received stating which Long balance sheet recognised security position is protected by which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Long non-balance sheet recognised security position collateral received assigment
DESCRIPTION: Long non-balance sheet recognised security position collateral received assigment is the combination of Long non- balance sheet recognised security position and collateral received stating which Long non- balance sheet recognised security position is protected by which Collateral.

NAME: Long non-balance sheet recognised security position protection arrangement received assignment
DESCRIPTION: Long non-balance sheet recognised security position Protection arrangement received assignment is the combination of Long non-balance sheet recognised security position Protection arrangement received and Protection arrangement received stating which Long non-balance sheet recognised security position is protected by which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Long/Short balance sheet recognised security position as a hedge
DESCRIPTION: Long/Short balance sheet recognised security position as a hedge is the role in which the Security position role acts as a hedge.

NAME: Long/Short balance sheet recognised security position
DESCRIPTION: A Long/Short balance sheet recognised security position is a balance sheet recognised security position that is either long or short.

NAME: Linked enterprise assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Linked enterprise is a combination of a Central bank and private sector company and a Central bank and private sector company that indicates which Central bank and private sector company is linked to which Central bank and private sector company in the sense of Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC.

NAME: Linked enterprise
DESCRIPTION: Linked enterprises are enterprises which have any of the relationships defined in Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC, Article 3 (3). (Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC)

NAME: Loan and advance Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Loan Collateral received assignment is the combination of a Loan and a Collateral received that indicates which Loan is assigned to which Collateral.

NAME: Loan and advance as a hedge
DESCRIPTION: Loan and advance as a hedge is a Loan and advance role where the Loan  and advance instrument acts as a non-derivative hedge.

NAME: Loan and advance
DESCRIPTION: A Loan and Advance is an Instrument that is either a Loan acording to Regulation (EU) 1071/2013 or an Advance according to Annex V, Part 2.85(g).

NAME: Security Issuer assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Security Issuer assignment is the combination of a Security and an Issuer that indicates which Security is issued by which Issuer.

NAME: Security
DESCRIPTION: A Security is a Security and Exchange tradable derivative attesting credit or the ownership of stocks or bonds.

NAME: Security lending component
DESCRIPTION: Security lending component is a Security/Security collateral lending component where the security is represented directly by the Security entity type.

NAME: Security lending component Security assignment
DESCRIPTION: Security lending component Security assignment is the combination of the Security lending component and the Security that indicates which Security has been lent out via the Security lending component.

NAME: Partner enterprise
DESCRIPTION: Partner enterprises are all enterprises which are not classified as linked enterprises and between which there is the following relationship: an enterprise (upstream enterprise) holds, either solely or jointly with one or more linked enterprises, 25 % or more of the capital or voting rights of another enterprise (downstream enterprise). (Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC)

NAME: Party code
DESCRIPTION: A party code is a code (different to the Party identifier) of a Party that identifies the party in systems outside of the bank. It is a combination of a Party and a Party code identifier.

NAME: Party
DESCRIPTION: A Party is an entity of interest.

NAME: Party previous period data
DESCRIPTION: A Party previous period data is information about a Party associated with the previous period. For example the Enterprise size that was calculated in the previous period.

NAME: Party role
DESCRIPTION: A Party role is a Party acting in a specific role. For example a Party acting in the role of Debtor (to a Loan).

NAME: Party risk data
DESCRIPTION: Party risk data is risk data related information associated with a Party.

NAME: Provisions associated with credit facility
DESCRIPTION: Provision associated with credit facility is provisions related to all commitments and guarantees, irrespective of whether their impairment is determined in accordance with IFRS 9 or their provisioning follows IAS 37 or whether they are treated as insurance contracts under IFRS 4. Under national GAAP based on BAD, provisions for ‘Commitments and guarantees given’ shall include provisions related to all commitments and guarantees.

NAME: Provisions associated with off-balance sheet item given
DESCRIPTION: Provision associated with off-balance sheet item given instrument is provisions related to all commitments and guarantees, irrespective of whether their impairment is determined in accordance with IFRS 9 or their provisioning follows IAS 37 or whether they are treated as insurance contracts under IFRS 4. Under national GAAP based on BAD, provisions for ‘Commitments and guarantees given’ shall include provisions related to all commitments and guarantees.

NAME: Provision
DESCRIPTION: A provision is a liability of uncertain timing or amount. (IAS 37)

NAME: Private sector company other than corporation
DESCRIPTION: An Central bank and private sector company other than corporation is an Central bank and private sector company that is not a Corporation. This type includes Non-profit institutions serving households according to the European system of accounts.

NAME: Past due debt security
DESCRIPTION: Past due debt security is a debt security past due in accordance with Part 2.48 of Annex V to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 680/2014.

NAME: Past due financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: Past due financial instrument is an Financial asset instrument whose payments are late, or past due.

NAME: Protection arrangement
DESCRIPTION: A Protection arrangement is an Arrangement that mitigates the credit risk that may arise from Contracts.

NAME: Qualifying central counterparty (QCCP)
DESCRIPTION:
A qualifying central counterparty (QCCP) is an entity that is licensed to operate as a CCP by the relevant
regulator and that is based and prudentially supervised in a jurisdiction where the
relevant regulator has implemented domestic rules for financial market infrastructures that are consistent with the PFMIs by
CPMI-IOSCO. (Basel Committee on Banking Supervision Capital requirements for bank exposures to central counterparties)

NAME: Register of Institutions and Affiliates Database (RIAD) party code
DESCRIPTION: Register of Institutions and Affiliates Database (RIAD) party code is an Other party code that is the RIAD code.

NAME: Rolling stock collateral
DESCRIPTION: Rolling stock collateral is collateral in the form of "transit vehicles such as buses, vans, cars, railcars, locomotives, trolley cars and buses, and ferry boats, as well as vehicles used for support services." (see Buy America regulation (49 CFR Part 661.3).

NAME: Real estate collateral located in a member state
DESCRIPTION: Real estate collateral located in a member state is Real estate collateral inside the borders of a members state.

NAME: Real estate collateral
DESCRIPTION: Real estate collateral is Registered collateral in the form of real estate.

NAME: Real estate collateral not located in a member state
DESCRIPTION: Real estate collateral not located in a member state is Real estate collateral that is not located inside the borders of a member state.

NAME: Renegotiated credit facility
DESCRIPTION: A Renegotiated credit facility is a credit facility where a renegotiation has occured.

NAME: Security borrowing component Security Collateral assignment
DESCRIPTION: Security borrowing component Security Collateral assignment is the combination of the Security borrowing component and the Security collateral that indicates which Security collateral has been borrowed via the Security borrowing component.

NAME: Security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative
DESCRIPTION: A Security position hedged by Over the counter (OTC) derivative is the combination of a Long/Short balance sheet recognised security position and an Over the counter (OTC) derivative as a hedge that indicates which (portion of a Long/short balance sheet recognised security position is hedged by which Over the counter (OTC) derivative (acting in the role of an Over the counter (OTC) derivative as a hedge).

NAME: Security position
DESCRIPTION: A Security position is the combination of a Security and an Investor that indicates which Investor has invested in which Security.

NAME: Security/Security Collateral lending component
DESCRIPTION: A Security/Security Collateral lending component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction component representing the Securities lent (to another Party), either as registered Security collateral, or directly as Security.

NAME: Security borrowing and lending transaction cash as collateral component
DESCRIPTION: A Securities borrowing and lending transaction cash as collateral component is a Securities borrowing and lending transaction including cash as collateral component that is cash as collateral.

NAME: Software collateral
DESCRIPTION:
Software as collateral is an Immaterial rights as collateral that is a legal concept that recognizes software as a form of intellectual creation that does not need a physical form, but grants the owner or creator exclusive rights to use, modify, distribute, or license it, subject to the intellectual property law.

See also IAS 38 for its usage as Property, Plant & Equipment or Other intangible non-financial assets.

NAME: Securities financing transaction (SFT)
DESCRIPTION:
Securities financing transaction (SFT) allows investors and firms to use assets, such as the shares or bonds they own, to secure funding for their activities.
A securities financing transaction can be:
• a repurchase transaction - selling a security and agreeing to repurchase it in the future for the original sum of money plus a return for the use of that money
• lending a security for a fee in return for a guarantee in the form of financial instruments or cash given by the borrower
• a buy-sell back transaction or sell-buy back transaction
• a margin lending transaction

NAME: Significant currency 10% depreciation contingent encumbrance
DESCRIPTION: Contingent encumbrance refers to the additional assets which may need to be encumbered when the reporting institutions faces adverse developments triggered by an external event over which the reporting institution has no control (including a downgrade, decrease of the fair value of the encumbered assets or a general loss of confidence). In these cases, the reporting institution will need to encumber additional assets as a consequence of already existing transactions. The additional amount of encumbered assets shall be net of the impact of the institution’s hedge transactions against the events described under the aforementioned stressed scenarios. (Annext 17 (Asset Encumbrance) 4. Part C)

NAME: Significant risk transfer securitisation
DESCRIPTION: Significant risk transfer securitisation is a Securitisation that establishes a significant risk transfer according to Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 243 (2) and Article 244 (2).

NAME: Ship collateral
DESCRIPTION: Ship collateral is Registered collateral in the form of a Ship (or parts of a Ship).

NAME: Short balance sheet recognised security position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Short balance sheet recognised security position International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is a Short  balance sheet recognised security position reported under IFRS.

NAME: Short balance sheet recognised security position
DESCRIPTION: A Short security position balance sheet is a Security position where the Investor (i.e. the holder of the Security position) sells the Security first with the intention to repurchasing it or covering it later (at a lower price).

NAME: Non-renegotiated financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Non-renegotiated financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument where no renegotiation has taken place.

NAME: Internal consolidation group
DESCRIPTION: An Internal consolidation group is an Internal group that consists of Parties that consolidated for a specific purpose, e.g. in order to create a consolidated balance sheet.

NAME: Credit spread risk (CSR) non-securitisation risk factor for standardised approach
DESCRIPTION:
Delta CSR non-securitisation: the CSR non-securitisation delta risk factors are defned along two dimensions:
(a) the relevant issuer credit spread curves (bond and CDS); and 
(b) the following tenors: 0.5 years, 1 year, 3 years, 5 years and 10 years.

NAME: Credit transfer other than securitisation and covered bond programme
DESCRIPTION: A Credit transfer other than Securitisation and Covered bond programme is a Securitisation and other credit transfer that is not a Securitisation or a Covered bond programme.

NAME: Currency collateral
DESCRIPTION: Currency collateral is Financial collateral in the form of currency.

NAME: Current tax asset
DESCRIPTION: A Current tax asset is a Tax asset according to IAS 1.54(n); IAS 12.5.

NAME: Asset pool Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool Debt security position assignment is the combination of an Asset pool and a Debt security position that indicates which (part of a) Debt security position is comprised in which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool (subject to a credit transfer other than securitisation and covered bond programme)
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool (subject to other credit transfer different than a Covered bond programme) is an Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer) that is associated with an other credit transfer different than Covered bond programme.

NAME: Natural person Key management personnel assignment
DESCRIPTION:
Natural person Key management personnel assignment is the combination of Key management personnel and Natural person that indicates which Natural person directly or indirectly influences the Key management personnel.

 If an individual is related to the entity based on the criteria stated above, all their close family members are also considered related parties. Close family members are defined as family members who are likely to influence, or be influenced by, that individual in their interactions with the entity (IAS 24.9). (via https://ifrscommunity.com/knowledge-base/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/#definition-of-a-related-party)

NAME: Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge
DESCRIPTION: An Over the counter (OTC) Derivative as a hedge is an Over the counter (OTC) Derivative role where the Over the counter (OTC) Derivative instrument acts as a hedge.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge is an Exchange tradable derivative position role that is applicable to those exchange tradable derivatives that is used in its role as a qualifying hedge.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position Protection arrangement received assignment
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position Protection arrangement received assignment is the combination of Exchange tradable derivative position and Protection arrangement received stating which Exchange tradable derivative position is protected by which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position role
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative position role is an Exchange tradable derivative position acting in a specific role.

NAME: Exchange tradable future
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable future is an Exchange tradable derivative in the form of a future.

NAME: Exchange tradable option
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable option is an Exchange tradable derivative in the form of an option.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative liability position derived data
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative liability position derived data is extra information about Exchange tradable derivative liability position instrument that can be derived from other information in the model.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative liability position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative liability position is an Exchange tradable derivative asset or liability position role where the Exchange tradable derivative position acts in the role of a liability position.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position
DESCRIPTION: An Exchange tradable derivative position is a Security or Exchange tradable derivative position with an Exchange tradable derivative.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS)
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) is an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge where the applicable accounting standard is IFRS.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP)
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge according to national general accepted accounting principles (nGAAP) is an Exchange tradable derivative position as a hedge where the applicable accounting standard is nGAAP.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative position Protection arrangement assignment
DESCRIPTION: Exchange tradable derivative position Protection arrangement assignment is the combination of Exchange tradable derivative position and Protection arrangement   stating which Exchange tradable derivative position is offering protection for which Protection arrangement.

NAME: Factoring cash reserve
DESCRIPTION: A Factoring cash reserve is a cash reserve of a Factoring transaction. If such a cash reserve is not represented as a collateral it is registered as a Factoring cash reserve.

NAME: Factoring
DESCRIPTION: Factoring is a Trade receivable in which the bank purchases receivables from a business and may advance all or part of the receivables.

NAME: Factor
DESCRIPTION: A Factor is a Party role where the Party provides a Factoring service to an Assigned debtor in a Factoring transaction.

NAME: Fundamental review of the trading book standard approach risk measure
DESCRIPTION: Fundamental review of the trading book standard approach risk measure is a measured risk of a position against a particular risk factor.

NAME: Fundamental review of the trading book standard approach risk measure for ETD positions
DESCRIPTION: A measured risk of an ETD position against a particular risk factor

NAME: Rating agency
DESCRIPTION:
A (Credit) Rating agency is a credit rating agency that is registered or certified in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1060/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 September 2009 on credit rating agencies or a central bank issuing credit ratings which are exempt from the application of Regulation (EC) No 1060/2009.
A Rating agency can be either an Extern Credit Assessment Institution (ECAI) or an Export Credit Agency (ECA).
An export credit agency (known in trade finance as an ECA) or investment insurance agency is a private or quasi-governmental institution that acts as an intermediary between national governments and exporters to issue export insurance solutions, guarantees for financing. The financing can take the form of credits (financial support) or credit insurance and guarantees (pure cover) or both, depending on the mandate the ECA has been given by its government. ECAs can also offer credit or cover on their own account. This does not differ from normal banking activities. Some agencies are government-sponsored, others private, and others a combination of the two.

NAME: Exchange tradable derivative

NAME: Instrument
DESCRIPTION:
An Instrument is a product that establishes a financial relationship between a bank and its customer.
In the context of accounting such a financial relationship may be considered a financial asset or a financial liabilty or an off-balance sheet item.

NAME: Instrument Protection arrangement assignment

NAME: Instrument role

NAME: Internal group role

DESCRIPTION:

DESCRIPTION: Investment property taken into possession is an investment property that was pledged by the debtor as collateral, but was obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt, whether on a voluntary basis or as part of legal proceedings.

NAME: Financial asset instrument debtor assessed
DESCRIPTION: A Financial asset instrument debtor assessed is a Potential retail exposure class financial asset instrument where a debtor based approach has been applied to evaluate the Default status.

NAME: Financial asset instrument derived data
DESCRIPTION: Financial asset instrument derived data is additional information about Financial asset instrument.

NAME: Financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION:
A Financial asset instrument is an Instrument role where the Instrument acts in the role of a Financial asset (according to the applied accounting standard) where the instrument is intended as an asset, either for the reporting agent or for someone else. 
Please note that a Financial asset instrument does not necessarily be recognised in the balance sheet.
Please note too that an instrument can be both an Asset and a Liability at the same time. This can happen, for example, when a debtor overpays the fees and/or installments.

NAME: Financial asset instrument individually assessed
DESCRIPTION:
A Financial asset instrument individually assessed is a Potential retail exposure class financial asset instrument where a Transaction based assessment of the Detault status has been applied in accordance with Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 178 Default of an obligor.
Regulation (EU) 575/2013, Article 178 Default of an obligor:
"In the case of retail exposures, institutions may apply the definition of default laid down in points (a) and (b) of the first subparagraph at the level of an individual credit facility rather than in relation to the total obligations of a borrower.".

NAME: Financial collateral
DESCRIPTION: Financial collateral is Collateral in the form of a financial asset.

NAME: Financial contract
DESCRIPTION: A Financial contract is a legally binding document under which one or multiple Instruments and / or Credit facilities are created.

NAME: Financial corporation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 549/2013, 2.55:
Definition: the financial corporations sector (S.12) consists of institutional units which are independent legal entities and market producers, and whose principal activity is the production of financial services. Such institutional units comprise all corporations and quasi-corporations which are principally engaged in: 
(a) financial intermediation (financial intermediaries); and/or 
(b) auxiliary financial activities (financial auxiliaries). 
Also included are institutional units providing financial services, where most of either their assets or their liabilities are not transacted on open markets.

NAME: Financial guarantee instrument not covering a Debt security

NAME: Financial guarantee instrument
DESCRIPTION:
A Financial guarantee instrument is an Off-balance instrument that is a Financial guarantee according to Annex V, Part 2, 81(c):
"'Financial guarantees received"  include contracts that require the issuer to make specified payments to reimburse the institution of a loss it incurs, because a specified debtor fails to make payment when due in accordance with the original or modified terms of a debt instrument."

NAME: Financial guarantee instrument Protection provider assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Financial guarantee instrument Protection provider assignment is an Instrument Entity role assignment where the Instrument is a Financial guarantee instrument and the Entity role is Protection provider.

NAME: Collateral given

DESCRIPTION: Contingent encumbrance refers to the additional assets which may need to be encumbered when the reporting institutions faces adverse developments triggered by an external event over which the reporting institution has no control (including a downgrade, decrease of the fair value of the encumbered assets or a general loss of confidence). In these cases, the reporting institution will need to encumber additional assets as a consequence of already existing transactions. The additional amount of encumbered assets shall be net of the impact of the institution’s hedge transactions against the events described under the aforementioned stressed scenarios. NAME: Instrument resulting from a Credit facility
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument resulting from a Credit facility is an Instrument that is created based on a Credit facility and not directly from a Financial contract.

NAME: Instrument resulting directly from a Financial contract
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument resulting directly from a Financial contract is an Instrument that is created directly as a result from a Financial contract without the involvement of a Credit facility.

NAME: Instrument Servicer assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Instrument Servicer assignment is the combination of an Instrument and a Servicer that indicates which Instrument is serviced by which Servicer.

NAME: Institutional unit
DESCRIPTION:
An Institutional unit is a Group which is the composition of Branches according to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, 2.12 and 2.13.
Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, 2.12:
2.12 Definition: an institutional unit is an economic entity characterised by decision-making autonomy in the exercise of its principal function. A resident unit is regarded as constituting an institutional unit in the economic territory where it has its centre of predominant economic interest if it has decision-making autonomy and either keeps a complete set of accounts, or is able to compile a complete set of accounts.

NAME: Internal consolidation group
DESCRIPTION: An Internal consolidation group is an Internal group that consists of Parties that consolidated for a specific purpose, e.g. in order to create a consolidated balance sheet.

NAME: Internal group
DESCRIPTION: An Internal group is a Group that comprises Parties that are related to the Reporting agent.

NAME: Internal group Key management personnel assignment
DESCRIPTION: Internal group Key management personnel assignment is the combination of Internal Group and Key management personnel that indicates which Key management personnel are part of the Internal group.

NAME: Internal group role
DESCRIPTION: A Internal group role is a role an Internal group may act in.

NAME: International organisation
DESCRIPTION:
An International organisation is an International organisation and General government drawing membership from more than one state, having activities in several states, and whose members are held together by a formal agreement.
Please note that this entity comprises multilateral development banks.

NAME: International organisation and general government
DESCRIPTION: An International organisation and general government is an Organisation that is either an International organisation or a General government.

NAME: Interest-only financial asset instrument
DESCRIPTION: A Interest-only financial asset instrument is a Financial asset instrument with an interest-only period.

NAME: Interest rate risk hedge portfolio
DESCRIPTION:
Interest rate risk hedge portfolio are the portfolio of instruments whose hedged postions need to be reported as one with the rows called 'Fair value changes of the hedged items in portfolio hedge of interest rate risk'.

See https://www.ifrs.org/content/dam/ifrs/meetings/2010/september/iasb/vbfi0910b14bobs.pdf

NAME: Inventory collateral
DESCRIPTION: Inventory collateral is Non-registered collateral in the form of inventory.

NAME: Investment property
DESCRIPTION: Investment property is property (land or a building or part of a building or both) held (by the owner or by the lessee under a finance lease) to earn rentals or for capital appreciation or both. (IAS 40.5)

NAME: Investment property taken into possession derived data
DESCRIPTION: Investment property taken into possession derived data is additional information for Investment property taken into possession that can be derived from other information in the model.

NAME: Investment property taken into possession
DESCRIPTION: Investment property taken into possession is an investment property that was pledged by the debtor as collateral, but was obtained in exchange for the cancellation of debt, whether on a voluntary basis or as part of legal proceedings.

NAME: Investment vehicle / fund
DESCRIPTION: An Investment vehicle / fund is a specific part of the balance sheet of an Organisation dedicated, and legally separated, for a specific purpose.

NAME: Investor
DESCRIPTION:
An Investor is a Party role where the Party invests in a position. 
Examples are the Investor in a Debt security position.
Please note that this definition also includes Investors as defined in Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2(11):
"'Investor' means a natural or legal person holding a securitisation position".

NAME: International securities identification number exchange tradable derivative
DESCRIPTION: An International securities identification number exchange tradable derivative is an Exchange tradable derivative with an International Securities Identification Number (ISIN).

DESCRIPTION: A Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) being a Financial guarantee is a Tranche in a synthetic securitisation without securitisation special purpose entity (SSPE) that is a Financial guarantee.

NAME: Tranche in a Traditional securitisation
DESCRIPTION:
Regulation (EU) 2402/2017, Article 2, (6):
´Tranche’ means a contractually established segment of the credit risk associated with an exposure or a pool of exposures, where a position in the segment entails a risk of credit loss greater than or less than a position of the same amount in another segment, without taking account of credit protection provided by third parties directly to the holders of positions in the segment or in other segments.

NAME: Collateral
DESCRIPTION: Collateral is an asset that is pledged to mitigate the credit risk that may arise from a contract that is not an Instrument.

NAME: Collateral given instrument Debt security issued assignment
DESCRIPTION: Collateral given instrument Debt security issued assignment is the combination of Collateral given instrument and Debt security issued that indicates which Debt security issued is protected by which Collateral given instrument.

NAME: Collateral role
DESCRIPTION: Collateral role is a role the Collateral may act in.

NAME: Credit facility Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Credit facility Collateral assignment is the combination of a Credit facility and a Collateral that indicates which Credit facility is assigned to which Collateral.

NAME: Credit facility Collateral received instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: A Credit facility Collateral received instrument assignment is the combination of a Credit facility and a Collateral received instrument that indicates which Credit facility is protected by which Collateral received instrument.

NAME: Asset pool Collateral received assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool Debt security position assignment is the combination of an Asset pool and a Debt security position that indicates which (part of a) Debt security position is comprised in which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer)
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool (subject to a Securitisation and other credit transfer) is a pool of assets that is subject to a Securitisation or other credit transfer. It may comprise Instruments or (parts of) Security positions that have been removed from the Reporting agents' balance sheet, e.g. in case of a Traditional securitisation using an SSPE, where the Reporting agents acts in the role of a Servicer.

NAME: Asset pool Exchange tradable derivative position assignment
DESCRIPTION: Asset pool Exchange tradable derivative position is the combination of an Asset pool and an Exchange tradable derivative position that indicates which (part of an) Exchange tradable derivative position is comprised in which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool Instrument assignment
DESCRIPTION: Asset pool Instrument assignment is the generalised combination of Asset pool and Instrument, that indicates which Instrument is part of which Asset pool.

NAME: Asset pool Long balance sheet recognised security position assignment
DESCRIPTION: An Asset pool long balance sheet recognised security position assignment is the combination of an Asset pool and a long balance sheet recognised security postion that indicates which (part of a) long balance sheet recognised security postion is comprised in which Asset pool.
